Action.desc: To define a new action, inherit from this class. Override the methods in this class to change the behavior of the action.

BarValue.desc: To define a new BarValue, inherit from this class and override some of the methods.

InputValue.desc: To define a new InputValue, inherit from this class, override some or all of the methods, and set the value of the default field.

Live2D.desc: This displayable displays a Live2D animation.
Live2D.signature: (filename, zoom=None, top=0.0, base=1.0, height=1.0, aliases=None, loop=False, fade=None, seamless=None, attribute_function=None, attribute_filter=None, update_function=None, default_fade=1.0, old_beziers=None, deduplication_key=None, **properties)

MultiPersistent.desc: Creates a new `MultiPersistent` object. This should only be called at init time, and it returns a new `MultiPersistent` with the given name.

Sample.desc: A sample function that doesn't actually exist in Ren'Py, but is used only in documentation.

Style.desc: `parent` The styles parent. This can be another Style object, or a string.

Transform.desc: Creates a transform which applies operations such as cropping, rotation, scaling or alpha-blending to its child. A transform object has fields corresponding to the `transform properties <transform_properties>`, which it applies to its child.

_.desc: (Single underscore) Returns `s` unchanged. Ren'Py will scan for strings enclosed in this function, and add them to the list of translatable strings. The strings will not be translated until they are displayed.

__.desc: (Double underscore) Returns `s` immediately translated into the current language. Strings enclosed in this function will be added to the list of translatable strings. Note that the string may be double-translated, if it matches a string translation when it is displayed.

___.desc: (Triple underscore) Immediately translates `s` into the current language. If a `text interpolation <text-interpolation>` is found, the interpolation will be performed using the local variables in the scope that called this function. Note that the string may be double-translated, if it matches a string translation when it is displayed.

_autosave.desc: This variable can be set to False to disable autosave.

_confirm_quit.desc: This determines if quitting the game asks for confirmation. It is set to False during the splashscreen, and is ignored when in the main menu.

_constant.desc: If set to true in a store, indicates the store is constant. See `constant-stores`.

_dismiss_pause.desc: If True, the player can dismiss pauses and transitions.

_game_menu_screen.desc: This is the screen that is displayed when entering the game menu with no more specific screen selected. (For example, when right-clicking, pressing escape, or when `ShowMenu` is not given an argument.) If None, entry to the game menu is disallowed.

_greedy_rollback.desc: Determines if the game performs a greedy rollback after a load. A greedy rollback will rollback to just after the last statement that interacted, rather than to just before the statement that the game was in during the load.

_history.desc: If true, Ren'Py will record dialogue history when a line is shown. (Note that `config.history_length` must be set as well.)

_history_list.desc: This is a list of history objects, corresponding to each line of history from oldest to newest. See the `History <history>` section for more information.

_ignore_action.desc: When this is not None, it's an action that is run after clicking Ignore on the error handling screen. The action is usually `Jump`, to jump the game to a place that can recover from an error. If None, control continues with the next Ren'Py statement.

_in_replay.desc: When in replay mode, this is sent to the label at which replay mode was started - the label that was called, not the one the call originated from. Outside of replay mode, this is None.

_live2d_fade.desc: If true, Live2D animations use motion fading. If False, animations are transitioned abruptly.

_menu.desc: Ren'Py sets this variable to True when entering a main menu or game menu context.

_preferences.language.desc: The name of the current language, or None if the default language is being used. This should be treated as a read-only variable. To change the language, call `renpy.change_language`.

_preferences.resource_path_translations.desc: A mapping from resource path prefixes to translated path prefixes. The mapping is applied by the loader before the normal global-language search.

_quit_slot.desc: If not None, this should be a string giving the name of a file slot. When Ren'Py quits, the game will be saved in this slot.

_scene_show_hide_transition.desc: If not None, this is a transition that will be performed using the with statement after a series of scene, show, and hide statements that are not followed by a with statement, or by a window transition.

_screenshot_pattern.desc: If not None, this string is used in preference to `config.screenshot_pattern` to determine the filename of a screenshot. Please see the documentation for that variable for the format of the string.

_test.focus_trials.desc: An integer specifying how many times the test system should try to find a valid spot to `move the mouse <test-move-statement>` when using a selector without a position. Defaults to `100`.

_test.force.desc: A boolean specifying whether to force the test to proceed even if `renpy.config.suppress_underlay` is `True`. Defaults to `False`.

_test.maximum_framerate.desc: A boolean specifying whether to use maximum framerate mode during tests. This will unlock the framerate beyond your screens refresh rate if possible. Defaults to `True`.

_test.screenshot_directory.desc: A string specifying the directory to store screenshots in. Defaults to `tests/screenshots`.

_test.timeout.desc: A float specifying the maximum number of seconds a test statement should wait for a condition to be met. Defaults to `10.0`.

_test.transition_timeout.desc: A float specifying the maximum number of seconds to wait for a transition to complete before skipping it and proceeding with the test. Defaults to `5.0`.

_test.vc_revision.desc: The version control (often git) revision of the current source tree, if available. Defaults to the `RENPY_TEST_VC_REVISION` `environment variable <environment_variables>`, or an empty string if not set.

_version.desc: This is set to `config.version` when a new game is started. It can be used by the `after_load` label or `config.after_load_callbacks` to determine which upgrades need to be done.

_window.desc: This set by the `window show` and `window hide` statements, and indirectly by `window auto`. If true, the dialogue window is shown during non-dialogue statements.

_window_auto.desc: This is set to true by `window auto` and to false by `window show` and `window hide`. If true, the window auto behavior occurs.

_window_subtitle.desc: This is appended to `config.window_title` to produce the caption for the game window. This is automatically set to `config.menu_window_subtitle` while in the game menu.

achievement.desc: A namespace that contains functions that grant and manage `achievements <achievement>`. This also contains much of the Steamworks integration.

achievement.steam.desc: If Steam initialized successfully, this is a namespace with high-level Steam methods. If Steam did not initialize, this is None. Always check that this is not None before calling a method.

achievement.steam_position.desc: If not None, this sets the position of the steam notification popup. This must be a string, one of "top left", "top right", "bottom left", or "bottom right".

activate_sound.desc: A sound that is played when the button is activated (clicked). This is also played when a bar or drag is activated.

adjust_spacing.desc: If True, Ren'Py will adjust the spacing of drawable-resolution text to match the spacing of the text rendered at virtual resolution, to ensure the size of frames and other containers holding text does not change.

adv.desc: This is a template ADV-mode character, and the default character kind that is used when `Character` is called.

align.desc: Equivalent to setting xalign to the first component of the tuple, and yalign to the second.

alt.desc: Alternative text used for the displayable when self-voicing is enabled. See the `self voicing <self_voicing>` section for more information.

altruby_style.desc: If not None, this should be a style object. The style that's used for alternate ruby text.

anchor.desc: Equivalent to setting xanchor to the first component of the tuple, and yanchor to the second component of the tuple.

antialias.desc: If True, the default, TrueType font text will be rendered anti-aliased.

area.desc: The tuple is interpreted as (`xpos`, `ypos`, `width`, `height`). Attempts to position the displayable such that it's upper-left corner is at `xpos` and `ypos`, and its size is `width` and `height`.

axis.desc: This allows the axes of a `variable font <variable-fonts>` to be set. If not None, this should be a dictionary mapping axis names to values. For example::

background.desc: A displayable that is used as the background of the window. This is often a `Frame`, allowing the size of the background to scale with the size of the window.

bar_invert.desc: If True, the value of the bar is represented on the right/top side of the bar, rather than the left/bottom side.

bar_resizing.desc: If True, we resize the sides of the bar. If False, we render the sides of the bar at full size, and then crop them.

bar_vertical.desc: If True, the bar has a vertical orientation. If False, it has a horizontal orientation.

base_bar.desc: A single displayable that is used for left_bar/right_bar or top_bar/bottom_bar, as appropriate. (This can be used with thumb to make a slider or scrollbar.)

black_color.desc: When rendering an image-based font, black will be mapped to this color. This has no effect for TrueType fonts.

blinds.desc: Transitions the screen in a vertical blinds effect lasting 1 second. An instance of the `ImageDissolve` transition class.

bold.desc: If True, render the font in a bold style. For a TrueType font, this usually involves synthetically increasing the font weight. It can also cause the font to be remapped, using `config.font_replacement_map`.

bottom_bar.desc: The displayable uses for the bottom side of the bar.

bottom_gutter.desc: The size of the gutter on the bottom side of the bar, in pixels.

bottom_margin.desc: The amount of transparent space below the displayable, in pixels.

bottom_padding.desc: The amount of space between the background and the bottom side of the window content, in pixels.

box_align.desc: This determines the alignment of rows or columns in a box. If 0.0, the default, rows are left-aligned and columns are top-aligned. If 0.5, it will center wrapped rows.

box_justify.desc: If not False, the contents of the box will be justified - that is, the items inside the box will have the spacing between them adjusted so they evenly span the size of the box. True will cause all lines but the final line to be justified. "first" will cause only the first line to be justified. "all" will cause all lines to be justified, including the final line. Justified lines do not obey box_align, except when there is only one item in a line.

box_reverse.desc: If True, the placement of the items in the box will be reversed. When this is True, a hbox will be filled right-to-left, and a vbox will be filled bottom-to-top. This defaults to False.

box_wrap.desc: If True, then boxes will wrap when they reach the end of a line or column. If False (the default), they will extend past the end of the line.

box_wrap_spacing.desc: When box_wrap is True, this is the spacing between wrapped lines or columns. (So it is the vertical spacing between lines in a wrapped hbox, and the horizontal spacing between columns in a wrapped vbox.)

bubble.area_property.desc: The name of the property that contains the area of the speech bubble. This is given as if it was supplied to `Character`, with the same prefixing system. By default, this is `"window_area"`, which means that the area is given as a property to the window displayable. Another useful choice is `"show_area"`, which will cause the area to be supplied as the `area` argument to the bubble screen.

bubble.clear_retain_statements.desc: This is a list of statements that will automatically cause retained bubbles to be cleared.

bubble.cols.desc: The granularity of the grid that's used to position and size speech bubbles, in the horizontal direction.

bubble.db_filename.desc: The database file, stored in the game directory, that contains the speech bubble information.

bubble.default_area.desc: This is the default area that speech bubbles are placed in, if no other area is specified. This is a tuple of the form (x, y, w, h), where each value is a number of grid cells.

bubble.expand_area.desc: This is a map from the name of a set of properties to a (left, top, right, bottom) tuple. If found in this set, the area of the speech bubble is expanded by the given number of pixels.

bubble.layer.desc: The layer that non-retained bubbles are placed on.

bubble.properties.desc: These are properties, apart from the area, that can be used to customize the speech bubble. This is a map from the name of a set of properties to a dictionary of properties and values. These properties supersede those given to the character, and are then supplied to the `bubble` screen.

bubble.properties_callback.desc: If not None, this should be a function that takes an image tag, and returns a list or tuple of property names that should be used for that image tag, in the order those names should be cycled through. This takes precedence over bubble.properties_order, and can be used to customize the list of bubble properties by character.

bubble.properties_order.desc: This is a list of the names of the sets of properties, in the order they should be cycled through in the speech bubble editor. If the names of the sets of properties are not given, the properties are cycled through in alphabetical order.

bubble.retain_layer.desc: The layer that retained bubbles are placed on.

bubble.rows.desc: The granularity of the grid that's used to position and size speech bubbles, in the vertical direction.

bubble:.desc: A namespace that contains variables that control the display of `dialogue bubbles <bubble>`.

build.allow_integrated_gpu.desc: Allows Ren'Py to run on the integrated GPU on platforms that have both integrated and discrete GPUs. Right now, this is only supported on Mac OS X.

build.android_permissions.desc: This is a list of strings, with each string giving the full name of an Android permission. For example, "android.permission.WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE". This simply declares that the application might request these permissions, it's necessary to use renpy.check_permission and renpy.request_permission as necessary to request the permission.

build.change_icon_i686.desc: If True, and icon.ico exists, the icon of the 32-bit Windows executable will be changed. If False, the icon will not be changed. Setting this to False may prevent some antivirus programs from producing a false positive for your game.

build.destination.desc: Gives the path to the directory the archive files will be placed in. This may be an absolute or a relative path. A relative path is considered to be relative to the projects directory.

build.directory_name.desc: This is used to create the names of directories in the archive files. For example, if this is set to "mygame-1.0", the Linux version of the project will unpack to "mygame-1.0-linux".

build.exclude_empty_directories.desc: If true, empty directories (including directories left empty by file archiving) will be removed from generated packages. If false, empty directories will be included.

build.executable_name.desc: This variable controls the name of the executables that the user clicks on to start the game.

build.game_only_update.desc: If true, `build.include_update` is enabled, and the "Game-Only Update for Mobile" package becomes available.

build.include_i686.desc: If true, files necessary to run on 32-bit x86 processors will be included in the Linux and Mac builds. If False, these files will not be included.

build.include_old_themes.desc: When true, files required to support themes that existed before Ren'Py 6.99.9 will be included in the build. When false, such files are excluded.

build.include_update.desc: When true, Ren'Py will produce the files required for the `updater <updater>` to work.

build.info.desc: This variable lets you store information that will be placed into the game/cache/build_info.json file in the built game. When the built game starts, game/cache/build_info.json is loaded and the contents placed into this variable.

build.itch_channels.desc: This maps a filename pattern (such as "\*-win.zip") to a string giving the itch channel the file should be uploaded to. This defaults to::

build.itch_project.desc: Setting this allows the Ren'Py launcher to upload your project to itch.io. This should be set to the name of a project registered with itch. (For example, "renpytom/the-question").

build.mac_info_plist.desc: This is a dictionary mapping strings to strings, that can be used to add or override keys in the mac's Info.plist file.

build.name.desc: This is used to automatically generate build.directory_name and build.executable_name, if neither is set. This should not contain spaces, colons, or semicolons.

build.time.desc: This variable defaults to None, but if your game has been built, it will be set to the time the game was built, in seconds since January 1, 1970.

build.update_formats.desc: This is a list of formats that the updater will build. The default, "rpu" is supported from Ren'Py 7.7 and 8.2 on. If you need to support updating using the earlier zsync-based updates, add "zsync' to the list.

build.version.desc: Gives a version of the build used by the build process. If None, this defaults to config.version. The main use of this is to allow config.version to have characters that are not valid in file or directory names.

build.wavedash_id.desc: When this is set to a non-empty string, the Ren'Py launcher writes a `wavedash.toml` file when building a web distribution. This file configures the distribution for upload to `Wavedash <https://docs.wavedash.com/engines/renpy>`_.

build:.desc: A namespace that contains variables that control the `build process <build>`.

caret.desc: If not None, this should be a displayable. The input widget will use this as the caret at the end of the text. If None, a 1 pixel wide blinking line is used as the caret.

center.desc: Centers horizontally, and aligns to the bottom of the screen.

child.desc: If not None, this gives a displayable that replaces the child of the button. For example, this (as insensitive_child) can be used to replace the contents of an insensitive button with an image that indicates the button is locked.

color.desc: The color the text is rendered in. When using a TrueType font, the font is rendered in this color. When using an image-based font, white is mapped to this color.

config.adjust_attributes.desc: If not None, this is a dictionary. When a statement or function that contains image attributes executes or is predicted, the tag is looked up in this dictionary. If it is not found, the None key is looked up in this dictionary.

config.adjust_view_size.desc: If not None, this should be a function taking two arguments, the width and height of the physical window. It is expected to return a tuple giving the width and height of the OpenGL viewport, the portion of the screen that Ren'Py will draw pictures to.

config.adv_nvl_transition.desc: A transition that is used to show the NVL-mode window when showing ADV-mode text directly after NVL-mode text.

config.afm_bonus.desc: The number of bonus characters added to every string when auto-forward mode is in effect.

config.afm_callback.desc: If not None, a Python function that is called to determine if it is safe to auto-forward. If None, an internal function is used to disable auto-forwarding when a voice is playing, unless `preferences.wait_voice` is set to False.

config.afm_characters.desc: The number of characters in a string it takes to cause the amount of time specified in the auto forward mode preference to be delayed before auto-forward mode takes effect.

config.afm_voice_delay.desc: The number of seconds after a voice file finishes playing before AFM can advance text.

config.after_default_callbacks.desc: A list of functions that are called (with no arguments) whenever default statements are processed. The default statements are run after the init phase, but before the game starts; when a save is loaded; after rollback; before lint; and potentially at other times.

config.after_init_callbacks.desc: A list of functions that are called (with no arguments) at the very end of the init phase, before the game starts normal execution for the first time. These are run after `config.after_default_callbacks`, and so this is t he place to set up callbacks that need access to default data. (The difference is that this is only run once, while `config.after_default_callbacks` is run after rollback and loading a save.)

config.after_load_callbacks.desc: A list of functions that are called (with no arguments) after a load occurs.

config.after_load_transition.desc: A transition that is used after loading, when entering the loaded game.

config.after_replay_callback.desc: If not None, a function that is called with no arguments after a replay completes.

config.all_character_callbacks.desc: A list of callbacks that are called by all characters. This list is prepended to the list of character-specific callbacks. Ren'Py includes its own callbacks at the start of this list.

config.allow_screensaver.desc: If True, the screensaver may activate while the game is running. If False, the screensaver is disabled.

config.allow_skipping.desc: If set to False, the user is not able to skip over the text of the game. See `_skipping`.

config.always_shown_screens.desc: A list of names of screens that Ren'Py will always show, even in menus, and when the interface is hidden. If a screen in this list is ever not shown, that screen will be re-shown. This is used by Ren'Py, which may modify the list.

config.archives.desc: A list of archive files that will be searched for images and other data. The entries in this should consist of strings giving the base names of archive files, without the .rpa extension.

config.audio_directories.desc: A list of directories that are searched for audio files and used to populate the `audio-namespace`.

config.audio_filename_callback.desc: If not None, this is a function that is called with an audio filename, and is expected to return a second audio filename, the latter of which will be played.

config.auto_channels.desc: This is used to define automatic audio channels. It's a map the channel name to a tuple containing 3 components:

config.auto_choice_delay.desc: If not None, this variable gives a number of seconds that Ren'Py will pause at an in-game menu before picking a random choice from that menu. We'd expect this variable to always be set to None in released games, but setting it to a number will allow for automated demonstrations of games without much human interaction.

config.auto_image_alt.desc: If True, images displayed without an explicit `alt` style property will be announced using their image name and attributes.

config.auto_load.desc: If not None, the name of a save file to automatically load when Ren'Py starts up. This is intended for developer use, rather than for end users. Setting this to "1" will automatically load the game in save slot 1.

config.auto_movie_channel.desc: If True, and the `play` argument is given to `Movie`, an audio channel name is automatically generated for each movie.

config.auto_screenreader_voicing.desc: If True, Ren'Py will automatically enable screen reader voicing on launch if an active screen reader (such as NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver, or Orca) is detected.

config.auto_voice.desc: This may be a string, a function, or None. If None, auto-voice is disabled.

config.automatic_oversampling.desc: The highest level of `automatic oversampling <automatic-oversampling>` that Ren'Py will use. If None, automatic oversampling is disabled.

config.automatic_steam_timeline.desc: If true, when run under Steam, the game will automatically update the Steam Timeline.

config.autoreload.desc: If True, Shift+R will toggle automatic reloading. When automatic reloading is enabled, Ren'Py will reload the game whenever a used file is modified.

config.autosave_callback.desc: A callback or list of callbacks or Actions that will be called after each time a background autosave happens. Although actions may be used, the Return action will not function.

config.autosave_frequency.desc: Roughly, the number of interactions that will occur before an autosave occurs. To disable autosaving, set `config.has_autosave` to False, don't change this variable.

config.autosave_on_choice.desc: If True, Ren'Py will autosave upon encountering an in-game choice. (When `renpy.choice_for_skipping` is called.)

config.autosave_on_input.desc: If True, Ren'Py will autosave when the user inputs text. (When `renpy.input` is called.)

config.autosave_on_quit.desc: If True, Ren'Py will attempt to autosave when the user attempts to quit, return to the main menu, or load a game over the existing game. (To save time, the autosave occurs while the user is being prompted to confirm his or her decision.)

config.autosave_prefix_callback.desc: If not None, this is a function that is called with no arguments, and return the prefix of autosave files. The default prefix used is "auto-", which means the autosave slots will be "auto-1", "auto-2", etc.

config.autosave_slots.desc: The number of slots used by autosaves.

config.basedir.desc: The full path leading to the game's base directory. This is a read-only variable. This is usually the directory above the `game/` directory. It contains logs like `log.txt` and on PC plaforms contains the executable used to launch the game. There is no guarantee any file will be there, as on Android files are stored inside the package.

config.before_load_callbacks.desc: A list of functions that are called (with no arguments) before a load occurs.

config.bottom_layers.desc: This is a list of names of layers that are displayed beneath all other layers, and do not participate in a transition that is applied to all layers. If a layer name is listed here, it should not be listed in `config.layers` or `config.top_layers`.

config.cache_surfaces.desc: If True, the underlying data of an image is stored in RAM, allowing image manipulators to be applied to that image without reloading it from disk. If False, the data is dropped from the cache, but kept as a texture in video memory, reducing RAM usage.

config.call_screen_roll_forward.desc: The value is used when the `roll_forward` property of a screen is None.

config.character_callback.desc: The default value of the `callback` parameter of `Character`.

config.character_id_prefixes.desc: This specifies a list of style property prefixes that can be given to a `Character`. When a style prefixed with one of the given prefix is given, it is applied to the displayable with that prefix as its ID.

config.choice_empty_window.desc: If not None, and a choice menu (usually invoked with the `menu` statement) does not have a caption, this function is called with the arguments ("", interact=False).

config.choice_layer.desc: The layer the choice screen (used by the menu statement) is shown on. If None, the screen's `layer` property is used, defaulting to "screens". This defaults to "screens" for games that declare compatibility with Ren'Py 8.5 or earlier.

config.clear_history_on_language_change.desc: If True, the history is cleared when the language changes. This is used to ensure that the history only contains strings that are representable in the current font. If False, the history is kept when the language changes.

config.clear_layers.desc: A list of names of layers to clear when entering the main and game menus.

config.clear_log.desc: If True, the log created by `config.log` is cleared each time Ren'Py starts.

config.conditionswitch_predict_all.desc: The default value of the predict_all argument for `ConditionSwitch` and `ShowingSwitch`, which determines if all possible displayables are shown.

config.console.desc: This enables the console in the case `config.developer` is not set to True.

config.context_callbacks.desc: These are callbacks that are called with no arguments when Ren'Py enters a new context, such as at the start of the game, when entering the game or main menus, or when beginning a replay.

config.context_clear_layers.desc: A list of layers that are cleared when entering a new context.

config.context_copy_remove_screens.desc: Contains a list of screens that are removed when a context is copied for rollback or saving.

config.context_fadein_music.desc: The amount of time in seconds Ren'Py spends fading in music when the music is played due to a context change. (Usually, when the game is loaded.)

config.context_fadeout_music.desc: The amount of time in seconds Ren'Py spends fading out music when the music is played due to a context change. (Usually, when the game is loaded.)

config.controller_blocklist.desc: A list of strings, where each string is matched against the GUID of a game controller. These strings are matched as a prefix to the controller GUID (which can be found in `log.txt`), and if matched, prevent the controller from being initialized.

config.custom_text_tags.desc: Maps text tag names to text tag functions, when the text tag can wrap other text.

config.debug_image_cache.desc: If True, Ren'Py will write information about the `image cache <images>` to image_cache.txt.

config.debug_prediction.desc: If True, Ren'Py will write information about and errors that occur during prediction (of execution flow, images, and screens) to log.txt and the console.

config.debug_sound.desc: Enables debugging of sound functionality. This disables the suppression of errors when generating sound. However, if a sound card is missing or flawed, then such errors are normal, and enabling this may prevent Ren'Py from functioning normally. This should always be False in a released game.

config.debug_text_overflow.desc: When True, Ren'Py will log text overflows to text_overflow.txt. A text overflow occurs when a `Text` displayable renders to a size larger than that allocated to it. By setting this to True and setting the `xmaximum` and `ymaximum` style properties of the dialogue window to the window size, this can be used to report cases where the dialogue is too large for its window.

config.default_attribute_callbacks.desc: When a statement or function that contains image attributes executes or is predicted, and the tag is not currently being shown, it's looked up in this dictionary. If it is not found, the None key is looked up instead.

config.default_language.desc: If not None, this should be a string giving the default language that the game is translated into by the translation framework.

config.default_tag_layer.desc: The layer an image is shown on if its tag is not found in `config.tag_layer`.

config.default_transform.desc: When a displayable is shown using the show or scene statements, the transform properties are taken from this transform and used to initialize the values of the displayable's transform.

config.defer_styles.desc: When True, the execution of style statements is deferred until after all `translate python` blocks have executed. This lets a `translate python` block update variables that are then used in style (not translate style) statements.

config.defer_tl_scripts.desc: When True, avoids loading scripts in the tl directory until the language is selected. See `deferred-translations`.

config.detached_layers.desc: These are layers which do not get automatically added to scenes. They are always treated as `sticky <config.sticky_layers>` and intended for use with the `Layer` displayable for embedding.

config.developer.desc: If set to True, developer mode is enabled. Developer mode gives access to the shift+D developer menu, shift+R reloading, and various other features that are not intended for end users.

config.disable_input.desc: When True, `renpy.input` terminates immediately and returns its `default` argument.

config.dispatch_gesture : Callable.desc: The function that is used to dispatch gestures. This function is passed the raw gesture string. If it returns non-None, the interaction ends.

config.display_start_callbacks.desc: This contains a list of functions that are called after Ren'Py displays a window, but before the first frame is rendered. The main use of this is to allow libraries to gain access to resources that need an initialized gui, like OpenGL functions.

config.emphasize_audio_channels.desc: A list of strings giving audio channel names.

config.empty_window : Callable.desc: This is called with no arguments when _window is True, and no window has been shown on the screen. (That is, no call to `renpy.shown_window` has occurred.) It's expected to show an empty window on the screen, and return without causing an interaction.

config.enable_language_autodetect.desc: If True, Ren'Py will attempt to determine the name of the language to use based on the locale of the player's system. If successful, this language will be used as the default language.

config.end_game_transition.desc: The transition that is used to display the main menu after the game ends normally, either by invoking return with no place to return to, or by calling `renpy.full_restart`.

config.end_splash_transition.desc: The transition that is used to display the main menu after the end of the splashscreen.

config.enter_replay_transition.desc: If not None, a transition that is used when entering a replay.

config.enter_sound.desc: If not None, this is a sound file that is played when entering the game menu.

config.enter_transition.desc: If not None, this variable should give a transition that will be used when entering the game menu.

config.enter_yesno_transition.desc: If not None, a transition that is used when entering the yes/no prompt screen.

config.ex_rollback_classes.desc: A list of class objects that should not generate a warning that the object supported rollback in the past, but do not now. If you have intentionally removed rollback support from a class, place the class object in this list and the warning will be suppressed.

config.exception_handler.desc: If not None, this should be a function that takes three arguments:

config.exit_replay_transition.desc: If not None, a transition that is used when exiting a replay.

config.exit_sound.desc: If not None, this is a sound file that is played when exiting the game menu.

config.exit_transition.desc: If not None, this variable should give a transition that will be performed when exiting the game menu.

config.exit_yesno_transition.desc: If not None, a transition that is used when exiting the yes/no prompt screen.

config.fadeout_audio.desc: The default audio fadeout time that's used to fade out audio, when audio is stopped with the `stop` statement or `renpy.music.stop`, or when a new audio track is started with the `play` statement or `renpy.music.play`. This is not used when queued audio begins.

config.failed_save_dump.desc: Similar to `config.save_dump`, but only triggers when the save fails.

config.fast_skipping.desc: Set this to True to allow fast skipping outside of developer mode.

config.file_open_callback.desc: If not None, this is a function that is called with the file name when a file needs to be opened. It should return a file-like object, or None to load the file using the usual Ren'Py mechanisms. Your file-like object must implement at least the read, seek, tell, and close methods.

config.file_slotname_callback.desc: If not None, this is a function that is used by the `file actions <file-actions>` to convert a page and name into a slot name that can be passed to the `save functions <save-functions>`.

config.fix_rollback_without_choice.desc: This option determines how the built-in menus or imagemaps behave during fixed rollback. The default value is False, which means that only the previously selected menu option remains clickable. If set to True, the selected option is marked but no options are clickable. The user can progress forward through the rollback buffer by clicking.

config.focus_crossrange_penalty.desc: This is the amount of penalty to apply to moves perpendicular to the selected direction of motion, when moving focus with the keyboard.

config.font_hinting.desc: This is a dictionary from a string containing the font filename to a string giving one of the font hinting modes in `hinting`. When `hinting` is True, the value is looked up in this dictionary, and the resulting mode is used.

config.font_name_map.desc: This is a map from (font name) to (font filepath/fontgroup). Font names simplify and shorten `{font}` tags, and gives them access to the `fontgroup` feature.

config.font_replacement_map.desc: This is a map from (font, bold, italics) to (font, bold, italics), used to replace a font with one that's specialized as having bold and/or italics. For example, if you wanted to have everything using an italic version of `Vera.ttf` use `VeraIt.ttf` instead, you could write::

config.font_size_adjust.desc: This is a dictionary mapping font names to size adjustments. The name is a string. The size adjustment may be a float, in which case it is multiplied with the original size. The size adjustment may also be a function that takes the filename (a string) and the original size (a float) as arguments, and returns the adjusted size.

config.font_transforms.desc: This is used to create new font transforms for accessibility purposes. The font transforms can be activated by `Preferences` using "font transform" as the first argument.

config.game_main_transition.desc: If not None, a transition that is used when returning to the main menu from the game menu, using the `MainMenu` action.

config.game_menu_action.desc: If not None, this is an Action that is run when the user asks to enter the game menu. This does not automatically start a new context - it's up to the action to do that.

config.game_menu_music.desc: If not None, a music file to play when at the game menu.

config.gamedir.desc: The full path leading to the game's `game/` directory. This is a read-only variable. There is no guarantee that any file will be there, as on Android files are stored inside the package.

config.gc_print_unreachable.desc: If True, Ren'Py will print to its console and logs information about the objects that are triggering collections.

config.gc_thresholds.desc: The GC thresholds that Ren'Py uses when not idle. These are set to try to ensure that garbage collection doesn't happen. The three numbers are:

config.gestures.desc: A map from gesture to the event activated by the gesture.

config.gl_blend_func.desc: A dictionary used to map a blend mode name to a blend function. The blend modes are supplied to the `gl_blend_func <gl-blend-func>` property, given below.

config.gl_clear_color.desc: The color that the window is cleared to before images are drawn. This is mainly seen as the color of the letterbox or pillarbox edges drawn when aspect ratio of the window (or monitor in fullscreen mode) does not match the aspect ratio of the game.

config.gl_lod_bias.desc: The default value of the `u_lod_bias <u-lod-bias>` uniform, which controls the mipmap level Ren'Py uses.

config.gl_program_cache.desc: If True, Ren'Py caches compiled OpenGL programs on disk for reuse on subsequent launches. This can reduce shader loading time on supported native renderers. Unsupported renderers compile shaders normally.

config.gl_resize.desc: Determines if the user is allowed to resize an OpenGL-drawn window.

config.gl_test_image.desc: The name of the image that is used when running the OpenGL performance test. This image will be shown for 5 frames or .25 seconds, on startup. It will then be automatically hidden.

config.glsl_version.desc: The version used by shader parts that don't pass `glsl` to `renpy.register_shader`. This defaults to 300 in new games and to 100 in games that declare compatibility with Ren'Py 8.5 or earlier.

config.hard_rollback_limit.desc: This is the number of steps that Ren'Py will let the user interactively rollback. Set this to 0 to disable rollback entirely, although we don't recommend that, as rollback is useful to let the user see text he skipped by mistake.

config.has_autosave.desc: If True, the game will autosave. If False, no autosaving will occur.

config.has_music.desc: If True, the "music" mixer is enabled. Audio channels will not be assigned the "music" mixer when this is False. The default GUI will hide the music mixer if this is False. When this, config.has_sound, and config.has_voice are all False, the default GUI will hide the main mixer as well.

config.has_sound.desc: If True, the "sfx" mixer is enabled. Audio channels will not be assigned the "sfx" mixer when this is False. The default GUI will hide the sound mixer if this is False.

config.has_voice.desc: If True, the "voice" mixer is enabled. Ren'Py's voice statement and other voice-related functionality will be disabled when this is False. Audio channels will not be assigned the "voice" mixer when this is False. The default GUI will hide the voice mixer if this is False.

config.help.desc: The default value for the `Help` action.

config.help_screen.desc: The name of the screen shown by pressing f1 on the keyboard, or by the `Help` action under certain circumstances.

config.hide.desc: A function that is called when the `hide statement <hide-statement>` is executed. This should take the same arguments as renpy.hide.

config.history_callbacks.desc: This contains a list of callbacks that are called before Ren'Py adds a new object to _history_list. The callbacks are called with the new HistoryEntry object as the first argument, and can add new fields to that object.

config.history_current_dialogue.desc: If True, the current dialogue will appear in the history screen.

config.history_length.desc: The number of entries of dialogue history Ren'Py keeps. This is set to 250 by the default gui.

config.hyperlink_handlers.desc: A dictionary mapping a hyperlink protocol to the handler for that protocol. A handler is a function that takes the value (everything after the :) and performs some action. If a value is returned, the interaction ends. Otherwise, the click is ignored and the interaction continues.

config.hyperlink_protocol.desc: The protocol that is used for hyperlinks that do not have a protocol assigned to them. See the `a` text tag for a description as to what the possible protocols mean.

config.idle_gc_count.desc: The net number of objects that triggers a collection when Ren'Py has reached a steady state. (The fourth frame or later after the screen has been updated.)

config.image_cache_size.desc: If not None, this is used to set the size of the `image cache <images>`, as a multiple of the screen size. This number is multiplied by the size of the screen, in pixels, to get the size of the image cache in pixels.

config.image_cache_size_mb.desc: This is used to set the size of the `image cache <images>`, in megabytes. If `config.cache_surfaces` is False, an image takes 4 bytes per pixel, otherwise it takes 8 bytes per pixel.

config.image_directories.desc: A list of one or more directories that Ren'Py searches for images, as described in the `images-directory` section. The directories are searched in order, and the first directory that contains the image is used.

config.image_extensions.desc: A list of file extensions that Ren'Py will use when searching for images, as described in the `images-directory` section.

config.imagemap_auto_function : Callable.desc: A function that expands the `auto` property of a screen language `imagebutton <sl-imagebutton>` or `imagemap <sl-imagemap>` statement into a displayable. It takes the value of the auto property, and the desired image, one of: "insensitive", "idle", "hover", "selected_idle", "selected_hover", or "ground". It should return a displayable or None.

config.implicit_with_none.desc: If True, then by default the equivalent of a `with None <with-none>` statement will be performed after interactions caused by dialogue, menus input, and imagemaps. This ensures that old screens will not show up in transitions.

config.input_caret_blink.desc: If not False, sets the blinking period of the default caret, in seconds.

config.interact_callbacks.desc: A list of functions that are called (without any arguments) when an interaction is started or restarted.

config.interface_layer.desc: The layer that built-in screens are shown on.

config.intra_transition.desc: The transition that is used between screens of the game and main menu. (That is, when the screen is changed with `ShowMenu`.)

config.keep_running_transform.desc: If True, showing an image without supplying a transform or ATL block will cause the image to continue the previous transform an image with that tag was using, if any. If False, the transform is stopped.

config.keep_screenshot_entering_menu.desc: If True, a screenshot taken with `FileTakeScreenshot` will be kept when entering the game menu. When False, a new screenshot will be taken just before menu entry.

config.keep_side_render_order.desc: If True, the order of substrings in the Side positions will be determine the order of children render.

config.keymap.desc: This variable contains a keymap giving the keys and mouse buttons assigned to each possible operation. Please see the section on `Keymaps <keymap>` for more information.

config.label_callbacks.desc: This is a list of callbacks that are called whenever a label is reached. The callbacks are called with two arguments. The first is the name of the label. The second is True if the label was reached through jumping, calling, or creating a new context, and False otherwise.

config.label_overrides.desc: This variable gives a way of causing jumps and calls of labels in Ren'Py script to be redirected to other labels. For example, if you add a mapping from "start" to "mystart", all jumps and calls to "start" will go to "mystart" instead.

config.language.desc: If not None, sets the language to use at game launch, overriding any memorized choice made by the user.

config.layer_clipping.desc: Controls layer clipping. This is a map from layer names to (x, y, height, width) tuples, where x and y are the coordinates of the upper-left corner of the layer, with height and width giving the layer size.

config.layer_transforms.desc: A dictionary mapping layer names to lists of transforms. These transforms are applied last, after `show layer` and `camera` transforms have already been applied.

config.layeredimage_offer_screen.desc: This variable sets the default value for the `offer_screen` property of layeredimages. See `the related section <layeredimage-statement>` for more information.

config.layers.desc: This variable gives a list of all of the layers that Ren'Py knows about, in the order that they will be displayed to the screen. (The lowest layer is the first entry in the list.) Ren'Py uses the layers "master", "transient", "screens", and "overlay" internally (and possibly others in future versions), so they should always be in this list.

config.lint_character_statistics.desc: If True, and `config.developer` is True, the lint report will include statistics about the number of dialogue blocks spoken for each character. The character statistics are disabled when the game is packaged, to prevent spoilers.

config.lint_hooks.desc: This is a list of functions that are called, with no arguments, when lint is run. The functions are expected to check the script data for errors, and print any they find to standard output (using the Python `print` statement is fine in this case).

config.lint_show_names.desc: If True, and `lint_character_statistics` is True, the lint report will expand the aliases of the character names to the name parameter given it `Character`, if possible.

config.live2d_old_beziers.desc: If True, live2d will by default use the old Bezier curve behavior, which usees easing. If False, the Cardano interpretation of beziers is used.

config.load_before_transition.desc: If True, the start of an interaction will be delayed until all images used by that interaction have loaded. (Yeah, it's a lousy name.)

config.load_failed_label.desc: If a string, this is a label that is jumped to when a load fails because the script has changed so much that Ren'Py can't recover. Before performing the load, Ren'Py will revert to the start of the last statement, then it will clear the call stack.

config.loadable_callback.desc: When not None, a function that's called with a filename. It should return True if the file is loadable, and False if not. This can be used with `config.file_open_callback` or `config.missing_image_callback`.

config.locale_to_language_function : Cal.desc: A function that determines the language the game should use, based on the user's locale. It takes 2 string arguments that give the ISO code of the locale and the ISO code of the region. These are normalized to lower case before this function is called.

config.locale_to_language_map.desc: This is a table used by the default implementation of locale_to_language_function. It maps (locale, region) pairs to language names. The default value of this table can be found in the locale symbol of `renpy/translation/__init__.py <https://github.com/renpy/renpy/blob/master/renpy/translation/__init__.py#L959>`_

config.log.desc: If not None, this is expected to be a filename. Much of the text shown to the user by `say <say-statement>` or `menu <menus>` statements will be logged to this file.

config.log_events.desc: If True, Ren'Py will log pygame-style events to the log.txt file. This will hurt performance, but might be useful for debugging certain problems.

config.log_gl_shaders.desc: If true, source code for the GLSL shader programs will be written to log.txt on start.

config.log_live2d_loading.desc: If True, loaded path and used motions and expressions will be written to log.txt on start.

config.log_width.desc: The width of lines logged when `config.log` is used.

config.longpress_duration.desc: The amount of time the player must press the screen for a longpress to be recognized on a touch device.

config.longpress_radius.desc: The number of pixels the touch must remain within for a press to be recognized as a longpress.

config.longpress_vibrate.desc: The amount of time the device will vibrate for after a longpress.

config.main_menu_music.desc: If not None, a music file to play when at the main menu.

config.main_menu_music_fadein.desc: The number of seconds to take to fade in `config.main_menu_music`.

config.main_menu_stop_channels.desc: A list of channels that are stopped when entering or returning to the main menu.

config.manage_gc.desc: If True, Ren'Py will manage the GC itself. This means that it will apply the settings below.

config.max_texture_size.desc: The maximum size of an image that Ren'Py will load as a single texture. This is important for 3d models, while 2d images will be split into multiple textures if necessary.

config.menu_arguments_callback.desc: If not None, this should be a function that takes positional and/or keyword arguments. It's called whenever a menu statement runs, with the arguments to that menu statement.

config.menu_clear_layers.desc: A list of layer names (as strings) that are cleared when entering the game menu.

config.menu_include_disabled.desc: When this variable is set, choices disables with the if statement are included as disabled buttons.

config.menu_window_subtitle.desc: The `_window_subtitle` variable is set to this value when entering the main or game menus.

config.mesh_oversample.desc: Determines how much mesh textures can be oversampled by. This, in turn, controls the maximum amount a mesh can be scaled up by before it introduces additional blurriness, at the risk of creating excessive large textures when a mesh is scaled up greatly.

config.minimum_presplash_time.desc: The minimum amount of time, in seconds, a presplash, Android presplash, or iOS LaunchImage is displayed for. If Ren'Py initializes before this amount of time has been reached, it will sleep to ensure the image is shown for at least this amount of time. The image may be shown longer if Ren'Py takes longer to start up.

config.mipmap.desc: This controls if Ren'Py generates mipmaps for images. If True, mipmaps are always generated. If "auto", mipmaps are generated only if the window is smaller than 75% of the virtual screen size. If False, mipmaps are never generated.

config.mipmap_dissolves.desc: The default value of the mipmap argument to `Dissolve`, `ImageDissolve`, `AlphaDissolve`, and `AlphaMask`.

config.mipmap_movies.desc: The default value of the mipmap argument to `Movie`.

config.mipmap_text.desc: The default value of the mipmap argument to `Text`, including text used in screen statements.

config.missing_image_callback.desc: If not None, this function is called when an attempt to load an image fails. The callback is passed the filename of the missing image. It may return None, or it may return an `image manipulator <im>`. If an image manipulator is returned, that image manipulator is loaded in the place of the missing image.

config.missing_label_callback.desc: If not None, this function is called when Ren'Py attempts to access a label that does not exist in the game. The callback should take a single parameter, the name of the missing label. It should return the name of a label to use as a replacement for the missing label, or None to cause Ren'Py to raise an exception.

config.mouse.desc: This variable controls the use of user-defined mouse cursors. If None, the system mouse is used, which is usually a black-and-white mouse cursor.

config.mouse_displayable.desc: If not None, this should either be a displayable, or a callable that returns a displayable. The callable may return None, in which case Ren'Py proceeds if the displayable is None.

config.mouse_focus_clickthrough.desc: If True, clicks that cause a window to be focused will be processed normally. If False, such clicks will be ignored.

config.mouse_hide_time.desc: The mouse is hidden after this number of seconds has elapsed without any mouse input. This should be set to longer than the expected time it will take to read a single screen, so mouse users will not experience the mouse appearing then disappearing between clicks.

config.movie_mixer.desc: The mixer that is used when a `Movie` automatically defines a channel for video playback.

config.name.desc: This should be a string giving the name of the game. This is included as part of tracebacks and other log files, helping to identify the version of the game being used.

config.narrator_menu.desc: If True, narration inside a menu is displayed using the narrator character. Otherwise, narration is displayed as captions within the menu itself.

config.nearest_neighbor.desc: Uses nearest-neighbor filtering by default, to support pixel art or melting players' eyes.

config.new_substitutions.desc: If True, Ren'Py will apply new-style (square-bracket) substitutions to all text displayed.

config.new_translate_order.desc: Enables the new order of style and translate statements introduced in `Ren'Py 6.99.11 <renpy-6.99.11>`.

config.notify : Callable.desc: This is called by `renpy.notify` or `Notify` with a single `message` argument, to display the notification. The default implementation is `renpy.display_notify`. This is intended to allow creators to intercept notifications.

config.nvl_adv_transition.desc: A transition that is used to hide the NVL-mode window when showing ADV-mode text directly after NVL-mode text.

config.nvl_choice_layer.desc: The layer the NVL choice screen is shown on. If None, the screen's `layer` property is used, defaulting to "screens". This defaults to "screens" for games that declare compatibility with Ren'Py 8.5 or earlier.

config.nvl_layer.desc: The layer the nvl screens are shown on.

config.nvl_list_length.desc: If not None, the maximum length of the list of NVL dialogue. This can be set (often in conjunction with forcing the dialogue to have a fixed height) in order to emulate an infinite scrolling NVL window.

config.nvl_page_ctc.desc: If not None, this is the click-to-continue indicator that is used for NVL mode characters that are at the end of a page. (That is, immediately followed by an nvl clear statement.) This replaces the ctc parameter of `Character`.

config.nvl_page_ctc_position.desc: If not None, this is the click-to-continue indicator position that is used for NVL mode characters that are at the end of a page. (That is, immediately followed by an nvl clear statement.) This replaces the ctc_position parameter of `Character`.

config.nvl_paged_rollback.desc: If true, NVL-mode rollback will occur a full page at a time.

config.old_substitutions.desc: If True, Ren'Py will apply old-style (percent) substitutions to text displayed by the `say <say-statement>` and `menu <menus>` statements.

config.open_file_encoding.desc: If not False, this is the encoding that `renpy.open_file` uses when its `encoding` parameter is none. This is mostly used when porting Python 2 games that used `renpy.file` extensively to Python 3, to have those files open as text by default.

config.optimize_texture_bounds.desc: When True, Ren'Py will scan images to find the bounding box of the non-transparent pixels, and only load those pixels into a texture.

config.overlay_during_with.desc: True if we want overlays to be shown during `with statements <with-statement>`, or False if we'd prefer that they be hidden during the with statements.

config.overlay_layers.desc: This is a list of all of the overlay layers. Overlay layers are cleared before the overlay functions are called. "overlay" should always be in this list.

config.overlay_screens.desc: A list of screens that are displayed when the overlay is enabled, and hidden when the overlay is suppressed. (The screens are shown on the screens layer, not the overlay layer.)

config.pad_bindings.desc: An equivalent of `config.keymap` for gamepads. Please see `keymap`'s section about pad bindings for more information.

config.pass_controller_events.desc: If True, pygame-like CONTROLLER events are passed to Displayables event handlers. If not, those are consumed by Ren'Py.

config.pass_joystick_events.desc: If True, pygame-like JOYSTICK events are passed to Displayables event handlers. If not, those are consumed by Ren'Py.

config.pause_after_rollback.desc: If False, the default, rolling back will skip any pauses (timed or not) and stop only at other interactions such as dialogues, menus... If True, Ren'Py will include timeless pauses to the valid places a rollback can take the user.

config.pause_with_transition.desc: If False, `renpy.pause` is always used by the `pause` statement. If True, when given a delay, `pause 5` is equivalent to `with Pause(5)`.

config.per_frame_screens.desc: This is a list of strings giving the name of screens that are updated once per frame, rather than once per interaction. Ren'Py uses this internally, so if you add a screen, append the name rather than replacing the list in its entirety.

config.periodic_callbacks.desc: This is a list of functions that are called, with no arguments, at around 20Hz.

config.persistent_callback.desc: When not None, a function that's called with a persistent store whenever a persistent save file is loaded. It should make any alterations in-place.

config.perspective.desc: The default value used when `perspective` is not set to a 3-tuple. `z` depends on the size of the game, as defined above.

config.physical_height.desc: If set, this is the default height of the window containing the Ren'Py game, in pixels. If not set, the height of the window defaults to `config.screen_height`.

config.physical_width.desc: If set, this is the default height of the window containing the Ren'Py game, in pixels. If not set, the width of the window defaults to `config.screen_width`.

config.play_channel.desc: The name of the audio channel used by `renpy.play`, `hover_sound`, and `activate_sound`.

config.pre_screenshot_actions.desc: A list of actions that are run before a screenshot is taken. This is intended to hide transient elements that should not be shown in the screenshot.

config.predict_shaders.desc: If True, shader combinations used by predicted displayables are compiled during expensive idle prediction.

config.predict_statements.desc: This is the number of statements, including the current one, to consider when doing predictive image loading. A breadth-first search from the current statement is performed until this number of statements is considered, and any image referenced in those statements is potentially predictively loaded. Setting this to 0 will disable predictive loading of images.

config.preload_fonts.desc: A list of the names of TrueType and OpenType fonts that Ren'Py should load when starting up. Including the name of a font here can prevent Ren'Py from pausing when introducing a new typeface.

config.preserve_volume_when_muted.desc: If False, the volume of channels are shown as 0 and changing it disables mute when the channel is mute. If True, the default, it is shown and adjustable while keeping mute.

config.profile.desc: If set to True, some profiling information will be output to stdout.

config.profile_init.desc: `init` and `init python` blocks taking longer than this amount of time to run are reported to log file.

config.python_callbacks.desc: A list of functions that are called, without arguments, whenever a Python block is run outside of the init phase.

config.python_exit_callbacks.desc: A list of functions that are called when Ren'Py is about to exit to the operating system. This is intended to be used to deinitialize Python modules.

config.quicksave_slots.desc: The number of slots used by quicksaves.

config.quit_action : Action.desc: The action that is called when the user clicks the quit button on a window. The default action prompts the user to see if they want to quit the game.

config.quit_callbacks.desc: A list of functions that are called without any arguments when Ren'Py is either terminating or reloading the script. This is intended to free resources, such as opened files or started threads, that are created inside init code, if such things aren't freed automatically.

config.quit_on_mobile_background.desc: If True, the mobile app will quit when it loses focus, rather than saving and restoring its state. (See also `config.save_on_mobile_background`, which controls this behavior.)

config.raise_image_exceptions.desc: If True, Ren'Py will raise an exception when an image name is not found. If False, Ren'Py will display a textual error message in place of the image.

config.raise_image_load_exceptions.desc: If True, Ren'Py will raise an exception when an exception happens during image loading. If False, Ren'Py will display a textual error message in place of the image.

config.reload_modules.desc: A list of strings giving the names of python modules that should be reloaded along with the game. Any submodules of these modules will also be reloaded.

config.renamed_files.desc: A map from file names to new file names. When Ren'Py looks for a file by one of the keys in this dictionary, it will instead look for the corresponding value. This is useful for handling files that have been renamed - for example, when font filenames change between versions of a bundled font. The keys must be lower-case and use forward slashes as path separators.

config.replace_text.desc: If not None, a function that is called with a single argument, a text to be displayed to the user. The function can return the same text it was passed, or a replacement text that will be displayed instead.

config.replay_scope.desc: A dictionary mapping variables in the default store to the values the variables will be given when entering a replay.

config.return_not_found_label.desc: If not None, a label that is jumped to when a return site is not found. The call stack is cleared before this jump occurs.

config.rollback_enabled.desc: Should the user be allowed to rollback the game? If set to False, the user cannot interactively rollback.

config.rollback_length.desc: When there are more than this many statements in the rollback log, Ren'Py will consider trimming the log. This also covers how many steps Ren'Py will rollback when trying to load a save when the script has changed.

config.rollback_side_size.desc: If the rollback side is enabled, the fraction of the screen on the rollback side that, when clicked or touched, causes a rollback to occur.

config.safe_text.desc: If True, Ren'Py will attempt to display text even if it contains errors, like unmatched text tags. If False, Ren'Py will raise an error when such text is encountered. This defaults to True in released games, and False in developer mode.

config.save.desc: If True, Ren'Py will allow the user to save the game. If False, Ren'Py will not allow the user to save the game, and will not show existing saves.

config.save_directory.desc: This is used to generate the directory in which games and persistent information are saved. The name generated depends on the platform:

config.save_dump.desc: If set to True, Ren'Py will create the file save_dump.txt whenever it saves a game. This file contains information about the objects contained in the save file. Each line consists of a relative size estimate, the path to the object, information about if the object is an alias, and a representation of the object.

config.save_json_callbacks.desc: A list of callback functions that are used to create the json object that is stored with each save and marked accessible through `FileJson` and `renpy.slot_json`.

config.save_on_mobile_background.desc: If True, the mobile app will save its state when it loses focus. The state is saved in a way that allows it to be automatically loaded (and the game to resume its place) when the app starts again.

config.save_persistent.desc: If True, Ren'Py will save persistent data. If False, persistent data will not be saved, and changes to persistent will be lost when the game ends.

config.save_physical_size.desc: If True, the physical size of the window will be saved in the preferences, and restored when the game resumes.

config.save_token_keys.desc: A list of keys that the game will trust when loading a save file. This can be used to allow the game's creator to distribute save files that will be loaded without displaying a warning.

config.savedir.desc: The complete path to the directory in which the game is saved. This should only be set in a `python early` block. See also `config.save_directory`, which generates the default value for this if it is not set during a `python early` block.

config.say_allow_dismiss.desc: If not None, this should be a function. The function is called with no arguments when the user attempts to dismiss a `say statement <say-statement>`. If this function returns True, the dismissal is allowed, otherwise it is ignored.

config.say_arguments_callback.desc: If not None, this should be a function that takes the speaking character, followed by positional and keyword arguments. It's called whenever a say statement occurs, even when the statement doesn't explicitly pass arguments. The arguments passed to the callback always include an `interact` argument, and include the others provided in the say statement (if any).

config.say_attribute_transition.desc: If not None, a transition to use when the image is changed by a say statement with image attributes.

config.say_attribute_transition_callback.desc: This is a function that return a transition to apply and a layer to apply it on

config.say_attribute_transition_layer.desc: If not None, this must be a string giving the name of a layer. (Almost always "master".) The say attribute is applied to the named layer, and Ren'Py will not pause to wait for the transition to occur. This will have the effect of transitioning in the attribute as dialogue is shown.

config.say_layer.desc: The layer the say screen is shown on. If None, the screen's `layer` property is used, defaulting to "screens". The resulting layer should be in `config.context_clear_layers`. This defaults to "screens" for games that declare compatibility with Ren'Py 8.5 or earlier.

config.say_menu_text_filters.desc: A list of functions that are given the text found in strings in the `say <say-statement>` and `menu <menus>` statements. Each is expected to return new (or the same) strings to replace them.

config.say_sustain_callbacks.desc: A list of functions that are called, without arguments, before the second and later interactions caused by a line of dialogue with pauses in it. Used to sustain voice through pauses.

config.scene.desc: A function that's used in place of `renpy.scene` by the `scene statement <scene-statement>`. Note that this is used to clear the screen, and `config.show` is used to show a new image. This should have the same signature as `renpy.scene`.

config.scene_callbacks.desc: A list of functions that are called when the scene statement runs, or `renpy.scene` is called. The functions are called with a single argument, the layer that the scene statement is called on. These functions are called after the layer is cleared, but before the optional image is added, if present.

config.screen_height.desc: The virtual height of the game, in pixels. If `config.physical_height` is not set, this is also the default size of the window containing the game. Usually set by `gui.init` to a much larger size.

config.screen_width.desc: The virtual width of the game, in pixels. If `config.physical_width` is not set, this is also the default size of the window containing the game. Usually set by `gui.init` to a much larger size.

config.screenshot_callback : Callable.desc: A function that is called when a screenshot is taken. The function is called with a single parameter, the full filename the screenshot was saved as.

config.screenshot_crop.desc: If not None, this should be a (`x`, `y`, `height`, `width`) tuple. Screenshots are cropped to this rectangle before being saved.

config.screenshot_pattern.desc: The pattern used to create screenshot files. This pattern is applied (using Python's %-formatting rules) to the natural numbers to generate a sequence of filenames. The filenames may be absolute, or relative to config.renpy_base. The first filename that does not exist is used as the name of the screenshot.

config.script_version.desc: If not None, this is interpreted as a script version. Ren'Py uses the script version to enable some compatibility features, if necessary. If None, we assume this is a latest-version script.

config.search_prefixes.desc: A list of prefixes that are prepended to filenames that are loaded. This is only used when a file is loaded or checked for being loadable. It does not affect scans of files used to automatically define images or namespace variables.

config.self_closing_custom_text_tags.desc: Maps text tag names to a self-closing text tag functions, when the text tag does not wrap other text.

config.shader_part_filter.desc: If not None, this is a function that is called with a tuple of shader part names. It should return a new tuple of shader parts that will be used.

config.show.desc: A function that is used in place of `renpy.show` by the `show <show-statement>` and `scene <scene-statement>` statements. This should have the same signature as `renpy.show`, and pass unknown keyword arguments unchanged.

config.side_image_change_transform.desc: If not None, a transform that is used when the new side image does not share the name image tag (or one of the new or old side images does not exist).

config.side_image_null.desc: The Null displayable to use when not displaying a side image. This can be changed, but only to other Null objects. One reason for doing so would be to set the side of the Null (eg. `Null(width=200, height=150)`) to prevent dissolves from being cut off.

config.side_image_only_not_showing.desc: When set to true, the side image will only show if an image with that tag is not already being shown on the screen.

config.side_image_prefix_tag.desc: If _side_image_prefix_tag is not None, it takes preference over config.side_image_prefix_tag.

config.side_image_same_transform.desc: If not None, a transform that is used when the new side image shares the same image tag as the previous side image.

config.side_image_tag.desc: If _side_image_tag is not None, it takes precedence over config.side_image_tag.

config.single_movie_channel.desc: If not None, and the `play` argument is give to `Movie`, this is the name used for the channel the movie is played on. This should not be "movie", as that name is reserved for Ren'Py's internal use.

config.skip_delay.desc: The amount of time that dialogue will be shown for, when skipping statements using ctrl, in milliseconds. (Although it's nowhere near that precise in practice.)

config.skip_indicator.desc: If True, the library will display a skip indicator when skipping through the script.

config.skip_sounds.desc: If True, non-looping audio will not be played when Ren'Py is skipping.

config.sound.desc: If True, sound works. If False, the sound/mixer subsystem is completely disabled.

config.sound_sample_rate.desc: The sample rate that the sound card will be run at. If all of your wav files are of a lower rate, changing this to that rate may make things more efficient.

config.speaking_attribute.desc: If not None, this should be a string giving an image attribute, which is added to the character's image tag when the character is speaking, and removed when the character stops.

config.special_directory_map.desc: This maps the special directory names ('images', 'audio', 'fonts') to a list of directories that will be searched for that kind of file. These are only used when loading a filename - for automatic definition of images and audiom see `config.image_directories` and `config.audio_directories`. New special directory names may be added in future versions of Ren'Py.

config.start_callbacks.desc: A list of callbacks functions that are called with no arguments after the init phase, but before the game (including the splashscreen) starts. This is intended to be used by frameworks to initialize variables that will be saved.

config.start_interact_callbacks.desc: A list of functions that are called (without any arguments) when an interaction is started. These callbacks are not called when an interaction is restarted.

config.statement_callbacks.desc: A list of functions that are called when a statement is executed. These functions are generally called with the name of the statement in question. However, there are some special statement names.

config.steam_appid.desc: If not None, this should be the Steam appid. Ren'Py will automatically set this appid when it starts. This needs to be set using the define statement::

config.sticky_layers.desc: A list of layer names that will, when a tag is shown on them, take precedence over that tag's entry in `config.tag_layer` for the duration of it being shown.

config.tag_layer.desc: A dictionary mapping image tag strings to layer name strings. When an image is shown without a specific layer name, the image's tag is looked up in this dictionary to get the layer to show it on. If the tag is not found here, `config.default_tag_layer` is used.

config.tag_transform.desc: A dictionary mapping image tag strings to transforms or lists of transforms. When an image is newly-shown without an at clause, the image's tag is looked up in this dictionary to find a transform or list of transforms to use.

config.tag_zorder.desc: A dictionary mapping image tag strings to zorders. When an image is newly-shown without a zorder clause, the image's tag is looked up in this dictionary to find a zorder to use. If no zorder is found, 0 is used.

config.textshader_callbacks.desc: This is dictionary that maps strings to callables. When `textshaders` with the string are used, the function is called to return a string giving another textshader. This can be used to make a textshader that changes based on a persistent variable, for example.

config.thumbnail_height.desc: The height of the thumbnails that are taken when the game is saved. These thumbnails are shown when the game is loaded. Please note that the thumbnail is shown at the size it was taken at, rather than the value of this setting when the thumbnail is shown to the user.

config.thumbnail_width.desc: The width of the thumbnails that are taken when the game is saved. These thumbnails are shown when the game is loaded. Please note that the thumbnail is shown at the size it was taken at, rather than the value of this setting when the thumbnail is shown to the user.

config.top_layers.desc: This is a list of names of layers that are displayed above all other layers, and do not participate in a transition that is applied to all layers. If a layer name is listed here, it should not be listed in `config.layers` or `config.bottom_layers`.

config.tracesave_screenshot.desc: If True, a screenshot is taken when a traceback save is made. If False, no screenshot is taken.

config.transform_uses_child_position.desc: If True, transforms will inherit `position properties <position-style-properties>` from their child. If not, they won't.

config.transient_layers.desc: This variable gives a list of all of the transient layers. Transient layers are layers that are cleared after each interaction. "transient" should always be in this list.

config.transition_screens.desc: If True, screens will participate in transitions, dissolving from the old state of the screen to the new state of the screen. If False, only the latest state of the screen will be shown.

config.translate_additional_strings_call.desc: A list of callbacks that are called when the translation system is searching for strings. Each callback is expected to be return and iterable or iterator of (filename, linenumber, string) tuples. The strings will then be treated as additional strings to translate.

config.translate_clean_stores.desc: A list of named stores that are cleaned to their state at the end of the init phase when the translation language changes.

config.translate_ignore_who.desc: A list of strings giving characters that will not have translations generated. This is useful for characters that are used for debugging or note purposes. This compares against string value of the expression in the statement. (So "e" will match `e` but not `l`, even if e and l are the same object.)

config.tts_substitutions.desc: This is a list of (pattern, replacement) pairs that are used to perform substitutions on text before it is passed to the text-to-speech engine, so that the text-to-speech engine can pronounce it correctly.

config.use_menu_text_filter.desc: If True, text in `menu <menus>` statements is passed through `config.say_menu_text_filter` and `config.say_menu_text_filters`. If False, menu text is left unchanged by those filters.
