config.variants.desc: A list of screen variants that are searched when choosing a screen to display to the user. This should always end with None, to ensure that the default screens are chosen. See `screen-variants`.

config.version.desc: This should be a string giving the version of the game. This is included as part of tracebacks and other log files, helping to identify the version of the game being used.

config.voice_callbacks.desc: A list of functions that are called by the voice system. The function should take two arguments:

config.voice_filename_format.desc: A string that is formatted with the string argument to the voice statement to produce the filename that is played to the user. For example, if this is "{filename}.ogg", the `voice "test"` statement will play `test.ogg`.

config.web_input.desc: If True, the web platform will use the browser's input system to handle `renpy.input`. If False, Ren'Py's own input system will be used. The browser's input system supports more languages, virtual keyboards, and other conveniences, but is not as customizable.

config.web_unload_music.desc: If not None, this should be an number of seconds. Music downloaded as part of `progressive downloading <progressive-downloading>` will be unloaded after this number of seconds.

config.web_video_base.desc: When playing a movie in the web browser, this is a URL that is appended to the movie filename to get the full URL to play the movie from. It can include directories in it, so "https://share.renpy.org/movies-for-mygame" would also be fine.

config.webaudio_required_types.desc: When running on the web platform, Ren'Py will check the browser to see if it can play audio files of these mime types. If the browser can, it is used to play the files. If not, a slower and potentially skip prone wasm decoder is used.

config.window.desc: This controls the default method of dialogue window management. If not None, this should be one of "show", "hide", or "auto".

config.window_auto_hide.desc: A list of statements that cause `window auto` to hide the empty dialogue window.

config.window_auto_show.desc: A list of statements that cause `window auto` to show the empty dialogue window.

config.window_hide_transition.desc: The transition used by the window hide statement when no transition has been explicitly specified.

config.window_icon.desc: If not None, this is expected to be the filename of an image giving an icon that is used for the game's main window. This does not set the icon used by windows executables and mac apps, as those are controlled by `special-files`.

config.window_show_transition.desc: The transition used by the window show statement when no transition has been explicitly specified.

config.window_title.desc: The static portion of the title of the window containing the Ren'Py game. `_window_subtitle` is appended to this to get the full title of the window.

config.with_callback.desc: If not None, this should be a function that is called when a `with statement <with-statement>` occurs. This function can be responsible for putting up transient things on the screen during the transition. The function is called with two arguments: the transition that is occurring, and the transition it is paired with. The latter is None except in the case of the implicit None transition produced by an inline with statement, in which case it is the inline transition that produced the with None. It is expected to return a transition, which may or may not be the transition supplied as its argument.

config:.desc: A namespace that contains variables that control the `configuration <config>` of Ren'Py. These variables should be set at init time (in `init python` blocks or with the `define`) and should not be changed once the game has started.

crop.desc: :type: None or (position, position, position, position) :default: None

default.desc: Centers horizontally, and aligns to the bottom of the screen. This can be redefined via `config.default_transform` to change the default placement of images shown with the show or scene statements.

default_mouse.desc: This is undefined by default. If defined, and if `config.mouse` is set at game startup, this is a key that is used to look up a mouse cursor when the current cursor does not exist, or is the default. This is used by `config.mouse` and `MouseDisplayable`.

define:.desc: The define namespace contains functions that define new variables, such as families of transitions.

depth.desc: Controls how many levels of nested tests the hook applies to.

description.desc: A string describing the test case. This is used in the test report.

director.audio_channel_patterns.desc: A map from a channel name to the list of audio patterns that are available in that audio channel. For example, if this is set to `{ 'sound' : [ 'sound/.opus' ], 'music' : [ 'music/.opus' ] }` the music and sound channels get their own lists of patterns.

director.audio_channels.desc: The name of the audio channels that can be used with the play, show and stop statements.

director.audio_patterns.desc: The default list of audio patterns that are used to match the files available in an audio channel.

director.button.desc: If True, the director displays a screen with a button to access the director window. If False, the game can provide it's own access, by making available the director.Start action.

director.director_spacing.desc: The spacing between two consecutive director lines.

director.other_spacing.desc: The spacing between two consecutive non-director lines.

director.scene_tags.desc: The set of tags that will be presented for the scene statement, and hidden from the show statement.

director.show_tags.desc: If not empty, only the tags present in this set will be presented for the show statement.

director.spacing.desc: The spacing between a director (scene, show, hide, with, play, queue, and voice) line and a non-director line, or vice versa. These spacings should be 0 or 1 lines, a higher spacing may not work.

director.tag_blacklist.desc: A blacklist of tags that will not be shown for the show, scene, or hide statements.

director.transforms.desc: A list of transforms that will be presented as part of the editor. In addition to these, any transform defined using the transform statement outside of Ren'Py itself will be added to the list of transforms, which is then sorted.

director.transitions.desc: A list of transitions that are available to the with statement. Since transitions can't be auto-detected, these must be added manually.

director.viewport_height.desc: The maximum height of scrolling viewports used by the director.

director.voice_channel.desc: The name of the audio channel used by voice.

director:.desc: The director namespace contains functions that control the `interactive director <director>`, which lets you insert images and music into the game interactively.

dissolve.desc: Takes 0.5 seconds to dissolve from the old to the new screen. An instance of the `Dissolve` transition class.

ease.desc: Also: *easeinright, easeinleft, easeintop, easeinbottom, easeoutright, easeoutleft, easeouttop, easeoutbottom*

emoji_font.desc: The font that's used to render Emoji characters. This is automatically used when a sequence of one or more Emoji are encountered, and no font text tag is in use.

enabled.desc: If this expression evaluates to `False`, this test is skipped. Defaults to `True`.

fade.desc: Takes 0.5 seconds to fade to black, and then 0.5 seconds to fade to the new screen. An instance of the `Fade` transition class.

first_indent.desc: The amount that the first line of text in a paragraph is indented by, in pixels.

first_spacing.desc: If not None, the spacing between the first and second members of this box, in pixels. This overrides the spacing property.

fit_first.desc: If True, then the size of the fixed layout is shrunk to be equal with the size of the first item in the layout. If "width", only the width is changed (the fixed will fill the screen vertically). Similarly, "height" only changes the height.

focus_mask.desc: A mask that's used to control what portions of the button can be focused, and hence clicked on. The type of this property determines how it is interpreted.

font.desc: A string giving the name of the font used to render text.

font_features.desc: If not None, this should be a dictionary mapping OpenType layout features to values. The keys of the dictionary should be the four-character OpenType feature tags, and the values should be booleans. For example::

foreground.desc: If not None, this displayable is drawn above the contents of the window.

gui.desc: The gui namespace contains functions that control the `default GUI system <gui>`. These variables only matter if you are using the default GUI system, and may not be used if you've replaced it. Define statements that affect the gui namespace are re-run when the translaton changes.

gui.FONT_SCALE.desc: A scaling factor that is applied to all text in the launcher.

gui.LIGHT_FONT.desc: The path to the font used for normal text in the launcher.

gui.REGULAR_BOLD.desc: If True, heavy-weight text is bolded.

gui.REGULAR_FONT.desc: The path to the font used for heavy-weight text in the launcher.

gui.accent_color.desc: The accent color is used in many places in the GUI, including titles and labels.

gui.bar_size.desc: The height of horizontal bars, and width of vertical bars.

gui.bar_tile.desc: If true, the bar images are tiled. If false, the images are linearly scaled.

gui.button_borders.desc: The borders surrounding a button, in left, top, right, bottom order.

gui.button_height.desc: The width and height of a button, in pixels. If None, the size is automatically determined based on the size of the text inside a button, and the borders given below.

gui.button_image_extension.desc: The extension for button images. This could be changed to .webp to use WEBP button images instead of png ones.

gui.button_text_insensitive_color.desc: The color of the button text in various states.

gui.button_text_size.desc: The font and size of the button text.

gui.button_text_xalign.desc: The horizontal alignment of the button text. 0.0 is left-aligned, 0.5 is centered, and 1.0 is right-aligned.

gui.button_tile.desc: If true, the sides and center of the button background are tiled to increase or decrease their size. If false, the sides and center are scaled.

gui.check_button_borders.desc: Increases the width of radio and check button borders, leaving extra space on the left for the check mark.

gui.choice_button_text_hover_color.desc: The color used for the text of focused choice buttons.

gui.choice_button_text_idle_color.desc: The color used for the text of unfocused choice buttons.

gui.confirm_frame_borders.desc: The borders applied to the fame used in the confirm screen.

gui.dialogue_text_xalign.desc: The horizontal alignment of dialogue text. 0.0 is left aligned, 0.5 is centered, and 1.0 is right-aligned.

gui.dialogue_width.desc: This variable gives the maximum width of a line of dialogue, in pixels. When dialogue reaches this width, it will be wrapped by Ren'Py.

gui.dialogue_ypos.desc: The horizontal and vertical positions of the actual dialogue. These are usually a number of pixels from the left or top side of the textbox. Setting a variable to 0.5 centers the dialogue in the textbox (see below).

gui.file_slot_rows.desc: The number of columns and rows in the grid of save slots.

gui.frame_borders.desc: The borders applied to frame windows.

gui.frame_tile.desc: If true, the sides and center of the confirm screen are tiled. If false, they are scaled.

gui.glyph_font.desc: A font used for certain glyphs, such as the arrow glyphs used by the skip indicator. DejaVuSans is a reasonable default for these glyphs, and is automatically included with every Ren'Py game.

gui.history_height.desc: The height of a history entry, in pixels. This can be None to allow the height of a history entry to vary at the cost of performance – config.history_length may need to be lowered significantly when this is None.

gui.history_spacing.desc: The amount of space to leave between history entries, in pixels.

gui.history_text_width.desc: The width of the name label and dialogue text, in pixels.

gui.history_text_xalign.desc: This controls the alignment of text and the side of the text that is aligned with xpos. 0.0 is left-aligned, 0.5 is center-aligned, 1.0 is right-aligned.

gui.history_text_xpos.desc: The horizontal positions of the name label and dialogue text. These can be a number of pixels from the left side of the history entry, or 0.5 to center.

gui.history_text_ypos.desc: The vertical positions of the name label and dialogue text, relative to the top of a history entry, in pixels.

gui.hover_color.desc: The color used by focused items in the GUI, including the text of of buttons and the thumbs (movable areas) of sliders and scrollbars.

gui.hover_muted_color.desc: Muted colors, used for the sections of bars, scrollbars, and sliders that do not represent the value or visible area. (These are only used when generating images, and will not take effect until images are regenerated in the launcher.)

gui.idle_color.desc: The color used for most buttons when not focused or selected.

gui.idle_small_color.desc: The color used for small text (like the date and name of a save slot, and quick menu buttons) when not hovered. This color often needs to be a bit lighter or darker than idle_color to compensate for the smaller size of the font.

gui.insensitive_color.desc: The color used by the text of buttons that are insensitive to user input. (For example, the rollback button when no rollback is possible.)

gui.interface_text_color.desc: The color used by static text in the game interface, such as text on the help and about screens.

gui.interface_text_font.desc: The font used for text for user interface elements, like the main and game menus, buttons, and so on.

gui.interface_text_size.desc: The size of static text in the game's user interface, and the default size of button text in the game's interface.

gui.kind_text_color.desc: If present, the color of the text.

gui.kind_text_font.desc: If present, the font used for the text.

gui.kind_text_size.desc: If present, the size of the text.

gui.label_text_size.desc: The size of section labels in the game's user interface.

gui.name_text_size.desc: Sets the size of character names.

gui.name_xalign.desc: The horizontal alignment of the character's name. This can be 0.0 for left- aligned, 0.5 for centered, and 1.0 for right-aligned. (It's almost always 0.0 or 0.5.) This is used for both the position of the namebox relative to gui.name_xpos, and to select the side of the namebox that is aligned with xpos.

gui.name_ypos.desc: The horizontal and vertical positions of the name and namebox. These are usually a number of pixels from the left or top side of the textbox. Setting a variable to 0.5 centers the name in the textbox (see below). These numbers can also be negative – for example, setting gui.name_ypos to -22 causes it to be places 22 pixels above the top of the textbox.

gui.namebox_tile.desc: These variables control the display of the frame containing the namebox.

gui.navigation_button_width.desc: Increases the width of navigation buttons.

gui.notify_frame_borders.desc: The borders of the frame that is used by the notify screen.

gui.notify_ypos.desc: The vertical position of the notify message, in pixels from the top of the window.

gui.nvl_borders.desc: The borders around the background of the NVL-mode. Since the background is not a frame, this is only used to pad out the NVL-mode to prevent it from pressing up against the sides of the screen.

gui.nvl_button_xalign.desc: The position and alignment of NVL-mode menu buttons.

gui.nvl_height.desc: The height of a single NVL-mode entry. Setting this to a fixed height makes it possible to have NVL-mode without paging, showing a fixed number of entries at once. Setting this to None allows entries to be of a variable size.

gui.nvl_spacing.desc: The spacing between entries when gui.nvl_height is None, and the spacing between NVL-mode menu buttons.

gui.nvl_thought_width.desc: The width of each kind of text, in pixels.

gui.nvl_thought_xalign.desc: The alignment of the text. This controls both the alignment of the text, and the side of the text that is placed at xpos. This can be 0.0 for left, 0.5 for center, and 1.0 for right.

gui.nvl_thought_xpos.desc: The positioning of character names, dialogue text, and thought/narration text, relative to the left side of the entry. This can be a number of pixels, or 0.5 to represent the center of the entry.

gui.nvl_thought_ypos.desc: The position of character names, dialogue text, and thought/narration text, relative to the top of the entry. This should be a number of pixels from the top.

gui.scrollbar_size.desc: The height of horizontal scrollbars, and width of vertical scrollbars.

gui.scrollbar_tile.desc: If true, the frame containing the bar of a scrollbar is tiled. If False, if it scaled.

gui.selected_color.desc: The color used by the text of selected buttons. (This takes priority over the hover and idle colors.)

gui.skip_frame_borders.desc: The borders of the frame that is used by the skip screen.

gui.skip_ypos.desc: The vertical position of the skip indicator, in pixels from the top of the window.

gui.slider_size.desc: The height of horizontal sliders, and width of vertical sliders.

gui.slider_tile.desc: If true, the frame containing the bar of a slider is tiled. If False, if it scaled.

gui.slot_button_borders.desc: The borders applied to each save slot.

gui.slot_button_height.desc: The width and height of the save slot button.

gui.system_font.desc: The font used for system text, like exception messages and the shift+A accessibility menu. This should be able to handle both ASCII and the game's translated language.

gui.text_color.desc: This sets the color of the dialogue text.

gui.text_font.desc: This sets the font that is used for dialogue text, menus, inputs, and other in-game text. The font file should exist in the game directory.

gui.text_size.desc: Sets the size of the dialogue text. This may need to be increased or decreased to fit the selected font in the space allotted.

gui.textbox_height.desc: The height of the textbox window, which should also be the height of gui/ textbox.png.

gui.textbox_yalign.desc: The placement of the textbox vertically on the screen. 0.0 is the top, 0.5 is center, and 1.0 is the bottom.

gui.title_text_size.desc: The size of the game's title.

gui.unscrollable.desc: This controls what to do if the bar is unscrollable. "hide" hides the bar, while None keeps it shown.

gui.vbar_borders.desc: The borders that are used with the Frames containing the bar images.

gui.vscrollbar_borders.desc: The borders that are used with the Frame containing the bar image.

gui.vslider_borders.desc: The borders that are used with the Frame containing the bar image.

hinting.desc: Controls how the font will be hinted. This should be one of the following strings:

hover_sound.desc: A sound that is played when the button gains focus.

hpunch.desc: When invoked, this transition shakes the screen horizontally for a quarter second.

hyperlink_functions.desc: This is a tuple of three functions relating to hyperlinks in text.

iap.desc: The iap namespace contains functions that control the `in-app purchase system <iap>`.

im.desc: *Note: Most functions in the im namespace are deprecated.*

instance.desc: When using a `variable font <variable-fonts>`, this can be a string giving a named instance of the font to use. For example, if the font has a "Bold" instance, this can be set to "Bold" to use that instance.

italic.desc: If true, the text will be rendered in italics. For a TrueType font, this usually involves synthetically increasing the font slant. It can also cause the font to be remapped, using `config.font_replacement_map`.

justify.desc: If True, additional whitespace is inserted between words so that the left and right margins of each line are even. This is not performed on the last line of a paragraph.

kerning.desc: A kerning adjustment, the number of pixels of space that's added between each pair of characters. (This can be negative to remove space between characters.)

key_events.desc: If True, keyboard-generated events are passed to the children of this button. If False, those events are not propagated. In this default style, this is set to True while the button is hovered, and False otherwise.

keyboard_focus.desc: If True, the default, this button can be focused using the keyboard focus mechanism, if it can be focused at all. If False, the keyboard focus mechanism will skip this button. (The keyboard focus mechanism is used by keyboards and keyboard-like devices, such as gamepads.)

keyboard_focus_insets.desc: If not None, this should be a tuple of four integers, giving the number of pixels that are used to shrink the left, top, right, and bottom sides of the focus rectangle, when it's used for keyboard focus.

language.desc: Controls the language family used to break text into lines, and for certain other text transformations. Legal values are:

layeredimage.desc: `Layered images <layeredimage>` are a way to combine multiple images into a single image, using attributes and conditions to control which images are shown. The layeredimage namespace contains classes that allow you to create and manipulate layered images from Python, the equivalent of the `layeredimage` statement.

layeredimage.predict_all.desc: Sets the value of `predict_all` for the ConditionSwitches produced by layeredimages' `if` statements.

layout.desc: Controls how words are allocated to lines. Legal values are:

left.desc: Aligns to the bottom-left corner of the screen.

left_bar.desc: The displayable used for the left side of the bar.

left_gutter.desc: The size of the gutter on the left side of the bar, in pixels.

left_margin.desc: The amount of transparent space to the left of the displayable, in pixels.

left_padding.desc: The amount of space between the background and the left side of the window content, in pixels.

line_leading.desc: The number of pixels of spacing to include above each line.

line_overlap_split.desc: When in slow text mode, and two lines overlap, this many pixels of the overlap are allocated to the top line. Increase this if the bottoms of characters on the top line are clipped.

line_spacing.desc: The number of pixels of spacing to include below each line.

main_menu.desc: Ren'Py sets this variable to True while in the main menu. This can be used to have screens display differently while in the main menu.

margin.desc: When given a two-item tuple, equivalent to setting xmargin and ymargin to the two items. When given a four-item tuple, equivalent to setting left_margin, top_margin, right_margin, and bottom_margin to the four items.

matrixcolor.desc: :type: None or Matrix or MatrixColor :default: None

matrixtransform.desc: :type: None or Matrix or TransformMatrix :default: None

maximum.desc: Equivalent to setting xmaximum to the first component of the tuple, and ymaximum to the second.

menu.desc: The function that's called to display the in-game menu. It should take the same arguments as `renpy.display_menu`, and pass unknown keyword arguments unchanged. Assigning `nvl_menu` to this will display an nvl-mode menu.

mesh.desc: :type: None or True or tuple :default: None

min_width.desc: Sets the minimum width of each line of that. If a line is shorter than this, it is padded to this length, with `textalign` used to specify where such padding is placed.

minimum.desc: Equivalent to setting xminimum to the first component of the tuple, and yminimum to the second.

mipmap.desc: This controls if textures created by this displayable are mipmapped. This applies only to certain displayables, including `Text`, `Movie`, and dissolves.

modal.desc: If True, the window is treated as modal. Events will stop propagating through layers while the mouse is within the window or button. If False, the window is not modal.

mouse.desc: The mouse style that is used when the button is focused. This should be one of the styles in `config.mouse`.

mouse_visible.desc: Controls if the mouse is visible. There are three values:

move.desc: Takes 0.5 seconds to the move images that have changed location to their new locations. An instance of the `MoveTransition` transition class.

name_only.desc: This is a template character that is used when a string is given as the character name in a say statement. This::

narrator.desc: This is the character that speaks narration (say statements that do not give a character or character name). This::

newline_indent.desc: If true, the `first_indent` indentation is used after each newline in a string. Otherwise, the `rest_indent` indentation is used.

offscreenleft.desc: Places the displayable off the left side of the screen, aligned to the bottom of the screen.

offscreenright.desc: Places the displayable off the right side of the screen, aligned to the bottom of the screen.

offset.desc: Equivalent to setting xoffset to the first component of the tuple, and yoffset to the second component of the tuple.

only.desc: If this expression evaluates to `True`, only this test case (and other tests with `only True`) will be run. Defaults to `False`.

order_reverse.desc: If False, the default, the items in the box will be drawn first-to-last, with the first item in the box being below the second, and so on. If True, this order will be reversed, and the first item in the box will be above all other items in the box.

outline_scaling.desc: This determines how outline sizes and offsets are scaled when the window is scaled.

outlines.desc: This is a list of outlines that are drawn behind the text. Each tuple specifies an outline, and outlines are drawn from back to front.
outlines.signature: list of tuple of (int, color, int, int)

padding.desc: When given a two-item tuple, equivalent to setting xpadding and ypadding to the two items. When given a four-item tuple, equivalent to setting left_padding, top_padding, right_padding, and bottom_padding to the four items.

parameter.desc: A variable name (or tuple of variable names) and a list of values (or list of tuples of values). The test will run once for each value (or tuple of values) in the list.

persistent.desc: The persistent namespace contains `persistent` data. Fields on this object start as None, and retain their values between runs of the game, even when not loading a save slot.

persistent._clear.desc: Resets the persistent data, except for fields starting with `__`.

persistent._hasattr.desc: Tests whether the `field_name` persistent field has been set or not. This allows you to distinguish fields that have been explicitly set to None from fields that have never been set.

perspective.desc: :type: True or False or Float or (Float, Float, Float) :default: None

pixellate.desc: Pixellates the old scene for .5 seconds, and the new scene for another .5 seconds. An instance of the `Pixellate` transition class.

point_to.desc: :type: (float, float, float), Camera, or None :default: None

pos.desc: Equivalent to setting xpos to the first component of the tuple, and ypos to the second component of the tuple.

prefer_emoji.desc: Some unicode characters have both Emoji and non-Emoji presentations. This style property chooses if such characters are given the Emoji presentation or not.

preferences.desc: The `preferences` namespace contains variables that contain preferences. While these can be read and set, the most common use is with the `default` statement, using syntax like::

preferences.afm_after_click.desc: If True, the auto-forward mode will be continued after a click. If False, a click will end auto-forward mode. The equivalent of the "auto-forward after click" preference.

preferences.afm_enable.desc: If True, auto-forward move is enabled, otherwise False. The equivalent of the "auto-forward time" preference.

preferences.afm_time.desc: The amount of time to wait for auto-forward mode. Bigger numbers are slower, though the conversion to wall time is complicated, as the speed takes into account line length. The equivalent of the "auto-forward" preference.

preferences.audio_when_minimized.desc: If False, audio channels are stopped when the window is minimized, and resumed when the window is restored. If True, window state will have no effect on audio. The equivalent of the "audio when minimized" preference.

preferences.audio_when_unfocused.desc: If False, audio channels are stopped when the window loses keyboard focus, and resumed when the window regains keyboard focus. If True, keyboard focus will have no effect on audio. The equivalent of the "audio when unfocused" preference.

preferences.desktop_rollback_side.desc: When on a desktop platform, touches or clicks to this side of the window cause rollback to occur. One of "left", "right", or "disable". This is the equivalent of the "rollback side" preference when on a desktop platform.

preferences.emphasize_audio.desc: If True, Ren'Py will emphasize the audio channels found in `config.emphasize_audio_channels` by reducing the volume of other channels. (For example, reducing the music volume when voice is playing.) If False, this doesn't happen.

preferences.force_mono.desc: If True, Ren'Py will mix stereo audio to mono before playing it. If False, stereo audio will be played normally.

preferences.fullscreen.desc: This is True when Ren'Py is in fullscreen mode, and False when it is running in a window. The equivalent of the "display" preference.

preferences.get_mixer.desc: Gets the volume for `mixer`. If the mixer is muted, this returns 0.0. The is returns a number between 0.0 and 1.0, where 0.0 is -40 dB (power) and 1.0 is 0 dB (power).

preferences.gl_framerate.desc: This is either an integer, or None. If not None, it's a target framerate that Ren'Py will attempt to achieve. If this is set low (for example, to 30), on a monitor with a high framerate (say, 60 frames per second), Ren'Py will only draw on every other frame.

preferences.gl_powersave.desc: This determines how often Ren'Py will redraw an unchanging screen. If True, Ren'Py will only draw the screen 5 times a second. If False, it will always draw at the full framerate possible.

preferences.gl_tearing.desc: This determines if tearing (True) or frameskip (False) is the preferred behavior when the game can't keep up with its intended framerate.

preferences.language.desc: The language that the player has selected to use when running the game. This is None for the default language or a string containing a language the game is translated to.

preferences.mobile_rollback_side.desc: When on a mobile platform, touches or clicks to this side of the window cause rollback to occur. One of "left", "right", or "disable". This is the equivalent of the "rollback side" preference when on a mobile platform.

preferences.mouse_move.desc: If True, the mouse will automatically move to a selected button. If False, it will not. The equivalent of the "automatic move" preference.

preferences.restore_window_position.desc: If True, Ren'Py will attempt to restore the window position when the game is restarted. If False, Ren'Py will not attempt to restore the window position. The equivalent of the "restore window position" preference.

preferences.set_mute.desc: Sets the mute setting for `mixer`. If `mute` is true, the mixer is muted. If `mute` is false, the mixer's volume is reverted to its value before it was muted.

preferences.show_empty_window.desc: If True, the window show and window auto statements will function. If False, those statements are disabled. The equivalent of the "show empty window" preference.

preferences.skip_after_choices.desc: If True, skipping will resume after a choice. If False, a choice will prevent Ren'Py from skipping. The equivalent of the "after choices" preference.

preferences.skip_unseen.desc: When True, Ren'Py will skip all text. When False, Ren'Py will only skip text that has been read by the player in any session. The equivalent of the "skip" preference.

preferences.system_cursor.desc: If True, the system cursor is forced to be used, ignoring the value of `config.mouse` and `config.mouse_displayable`. If False, it will not. The equivalent of the "system cursor" preference.

preferences.text_cps.desc: The speed of text display. 0 is infinite, otherwise this is the number of characters per second to show. The equivalent of the "text speed" preference.

preferences.transitions.desc: Determines which transitions should be shown. 2 shows all transitions, 0 shows no transitions. (1 is reserved.) The equivalent of the "transitions" preference.

preferences.tts_speed.desc: The speed of self-voicing. This is a number between 1.0 and 3.0, with 1.0 being the slowest and 3.0 being the fastest. The equivalent of the "self voicing speed" preference.

preferences.tts_voice.desc: The name of the self-voicing voice to use. If None, the default voice is used. The equivalent of the "self voicing voice" preference. The precise set of voices available varies by platform, and computer within the platform. For any given computer, `renpy.get_tts_voices` returns possible values this can be set to.

preferences.video_image_fallback.desc: If True, images are displayed instead of videosprites. If False, video sprites are displayed normally. The equivalent (inverted) of the "video sprites" preference.

preferences.voice_after_game_menu.desc: If True, voice will continue playing after the game menu is shown. If False, voice will be stopped when the game menu is shown. The equivalent of the "voice after menu" preference.

preferences.voice_sustain.desc: If True, voice keeps playing until finished, or another voice line replaces it. If False, the voice line ends when the line of dialogue advances. The equivalent of the "voice sustain" preference.

preferences.volume.desc: The `preferences` namespace contains variables that set the default volumes for each mixer. These should be set using the `default` statement, like::

preferences.volume.main.desc: The default volume of the main mixer, which is applied to all channels in addition to the per-channel mixer.This should be a number between 0.0 and 1.0, with 1.0 being full volume.

preferences.volume.music.desc: The default volume of the music mixer, which is used for the music and movie channels. This should be a number between 0.0 and 1.0, with 1.0 being full volume.

preferences.volume.sfx.desc: The default volume of the sfx mixer, which is used for the sound and audio channels. This should be a number between 0.0 and 1.0, with 1.0 being full volume.

preferences.volume.voice.desc: The default volume of the voice mixer, which is used for the voice channel (and hence the voice statement, auto-voice, etc.). This should be a number between 0.0 and 1.0, with 1.0 being full volume.

preferences.wait_voice.desc: If True, auto-forward mode will wait for voice files and self-voicing to finish before advancing. If False, it will not. The equivalent of the "wait for voice" preference.

preferences.web_cache_preload.desc: If True the game files will be loaded into the web browser's cache, allowing the game to be played offline. If False, the game files will not be loaded into the web browser's cache, and the game will require internet access to play. The equivalent of the "web cache preload" preference.

python_dict.desc: The python_dict class is the Python built-in dict class.

python_list.desc: The python_list class is the Python built-in list class.

python_set.desc: The python_set class is the Python built-in set class.

reading_order.desc: This controls the how text is presented for reading when RTL support has been enabled. The main use of this is to influence directionally neutral lines, such as those made up purely of punctuation.

renpy.desc: The renpy namespace contains function and classes that are part of the Ren'Py engine itself. These can be the equivalent of Ren'Py language statements, or can introduce functionality that does not merit a dedicated statement.

renpy.add_layer.desc: Adds a new layer to the screen. If the layer already exists, this function does nothing.

renpy.add_to_all_stores.desc: Adds the `value` by the `name` to all creator defined namespaces. If the name already exist in that namespace - do nothing for it.

renpy.android.desc: Has a true value when running on Android.

renpy.arguments.register_command.desc: Registers a command that can be invoked when Ren'Py is run on the command line. When the command is run, `function` is called with no arguments.

renpy.audio.filter.desc: The renpy.audio.filter namespace contains classes and functions that create `audio filters <audio_filters>`.

renpy.block_rollback.desc: Prevents the game from rolling back to before the current statement.

renpy.call.desc: Causes the current Ren'Py statement to terminate, and a jump to a `label` to occur. When the jump returns, control will be passed to the statement following the current statement.

renpy.call_screen.desc: The programmatic equivalent of the call screen statement.

renpy.call_stack_depth.desc: Returns the depth of the call stack of the current context - the number of calls that have run without being returned from or popped from the call stack.

renpy.can_fullscreen.desc: Returns True if the current platform supports fullscreen mode, False otherwise.

renpy.can_rollback.desc: Returns true if we can rollback.

renpy.can_show.desc: Determines if `name` can be used to show an image. This interprets `name` as a tag and attributes. This is combined with the attributes of the currently-showing image with `tag` on `layer` to try to determine a unique image to show. If a unique image can be show, returns the name of that image as a tuple. Otherwise, returns None.

renpy.cancel_gesture.desc: Cancels the current gesture, preventing the gesture from being recognized. This should be called by displayables that have gesture-like behavior.

renpy.change_zorder.desc: Changes the zorder of `tag` on `layer` to `zorder`.

renpy.check_permission.desc: Checks to see if an Android permission has been granted to this application.

renpy.checkpoint.desc: Makes the current statement a checkpoint that the user can rollback to. Once this function has been called, there should be no more interaction with the user in the current statement.

renpy.choice_for_skipping.desc: Tells Ren'Py that a choice is coming up soon. This currently has two effects:

renpy.clear_attributes.desc: Clears all image attributes for the `tag` image. If the tag had no attached image attributes, this does nothing.

renpy.confirm.desc: This causes the a yes/no prompt screen with the given message to be displayed, and dismissed when the player hits yes or no.

renpy.context.desc: Returns an object that is unique to the current context. The object is copied when entering a new context, but changes to the copy do not change the original.

renpy.context_dynamic.desc: This can be given one or more variable names as arguments. This makes the variables dynamically scoped to the current context. When returning to the prior context, the variables will be reset to the value they had when this function was called.

renpy.context_nesting_level.desc: Returns the nesting level of the current context. This is 0 for the outermost context (the context that is saved, loaded, and rolled-back), and is non-zero in other contexts, such as menu and replay contexts.

renpy.copy_images.desc: Copies images beginning with one prefix to images beginning with another. For example::

renpy.count_dialogue_blocks.desc: Returns the number of dialogue blocks in the game's original language.

renpy.count_displayables_in_layer.desc: Returns how many displayables are in the supplied layer.

renpy.count_newly_seen_dialogue_blocks.desc: Returns the number of dialogue blocks the user has seen for the first time during this session.

renpy.count_seen_dialogue_blocks.desc: Returns the number of dialogue blocks the user has seen in any play-through of the current game.

renpy.default_layer.desc: If layer is not None, returns it. Otherwise, interprets `tag` as a name or tag, then looks up what the default layer for that tag is, and returns the result.

renpy.display_menu.desc: This displays a menu to the user. `items` should be a list of 2-item tuples. In each tuple, the first item is a textual label, and the second item is the value to be returned if that item is selected. If the value is None, the first item is used as a menu caption.

renpy.display_reset.desc: Causes the display to be restarted at the start of the next interaction.

renpy.dynamic.desc: This can be given one or more variable names as arguments. This makes the variables dynamically scoped to the current call. When the call returns, the variables will be reset to the value they had when this function was called.

renpy.emscripten.desc: Has a true value when running in the browser. That value is specifically the emscripten module that lets you interact with the browser, see `renpy.emscripten.run_script` and similar functions.

renpy.emscripten.run_script.desc: Runs the given Javascript script. This does not return a result.

renpy.emscripten.run_script_int.desc: Runs the given Javascript script, and returns its result as an integer.

renpy.emscripten.run_script_string.desc: Runs the given Javascript script, and returns its result as a string.

renpy.end_interaction.desc: If `value` is not None, immediately ends the current interaction, causing the interaction to return `value`. If `value` is None, does nothing.

renpy.end_replay.desc: If we're in a replay, ends the replay immediately. Otherwise, does nothing.

renpy.error.desc: Reports `msg`, a string, as an error for the user. This is logged as a parse or lint error when approprate, and otherwise it is raised as an exception.

renpy.exists.desc: Returns true if the given filename can be found in the searchpath. This only works if a physical file exists on disk. It won't find the file if it's inside of an archive.

renpy.expand_predict.desc: Use the fnmatch function to expland `d` for the purposes of prediction.

renpy.fetch.desc: This performs an HTTP (or HTTPS) request to the given URL, and returns the content of that request. If it fails, raises a FetchError exception, with text that describes the failure. (But may not be suitable for presentation to the user.)
renpy.fetch.signature: (url, method=None, data=None, json=None, content_type=None, timeout=5, result='bytes', params=None, headers={})

renpy.fetch_emscripten.desc: Used by fetch on emscripten systems.

renpy.fetch_pause.desc: Called by the fetch functions to pause for a short amount of time.

renpy.fetch_requests.desc: Used by fetch on non-emscripten systems.

renpy.file.desc: An alias for `renpy.open_file`, for compatibility with older versions of Ren'Py.

renpy.filename_line_override.desc: Temporarily overrides the filename and line number. This is a context manager, use it like::

renpy.fix_rollback.desc: Prevents the user from changing decisions made before the current statement.

renpy.flush_cache_file.desc: This flushes all image cache entries that refer to the file `fn`. This may be called when an image file changes on disk to force Ren'Py to use the new version.

renpy.force_full_redraw.desc: Forces the screen to be redrawn in full. Call this after using pygame to redraw the screen directly.

renpy.free_memory.desc: Attempts to free some memory. Useful before running a renpygame-based minigame.

renpy.fsdecode.desc: Converts s from filesystem encoding to unicode.

renpy.fsencode.desc: Converts s from unicode to the filesystem encoding.

renpy.full_restart.desc: Causes Ren'Py to restart, returning the user to the main menu.

renpy.get_adjustment.desc: Given `bar_value`, a `BarValue`, returns the `ui.adjustment` it uses. The adjustment has the following attributes defined:

renpy.get_all_labels.desc: Returns the set of all labels defined in the program, including labels defined for internal use in the libraries.

renpy.get_at_list.desc: Returns the list of transforms being applied to the image with tag `name` on `layer`. Returns an empty list if no transforms are being applied, or None if the image is not shown.

renpy.get_attributes.desc: Return a tuple giving the image attributes for the image `tag`. If the image tag has not had any attributes associated since the last time it was hidden, returns `if_hidden`.

renpy.get_clipboard_data.desc: Returns the clipboard data for `mime_type`, or raises an exception if no data is available for that MIME type.

renpy.get_clipboard_mime_types.desc: Returns a list of MIME type strings currently available on the clipboard.

renpy.get_clipboard_text.desc: Returns the text currently on the clipboard, or raises an exception if no text is available.

renpy.get_editable_input_value.desc: Returns the current input value, and a flag that is true if it is editable. and false otherwise.

renpy.get_fetch_emscripten_progress.desc: Returns the fetch progress on emscripten systems as a float between 0.0 and 1.0.

renpy.get_fetch_progress.desc: Returns the progress of the currently active fetch requests as a float between 0.0 and 1.0. If no fetches are in progress, returns 1.0.

renpy.get_fetch_requests_progress.desc: Returns the progress of the currently active fetch requests as a float between 0.0 and 1.0. If no fetches are in progress, returns 1.0.

renpy.get_filename_line.desc: Returns a pair giving the filename and line number of the current statement.

renpy.get_hidden_tags.desc: Returns the set of image tags on `layer` that are currently hidden, but still have attribute information associated with them.

renpy.get_identifier_checkpoints.desc: Given a rollback_identifier from a HistoryEntry object, returns the number of checkpoints that need to be passed to `renpy.rollback` to reach that identifier. Returns None of the identifier is not in the rollback history.

renpy.get_image_bounds.desc: If an image with `tag` exists on `layer`, returns the bounding box of that image. Returns None if the image is not found.

renpy.get_image_load_log.desc: A generator that yields a log of image loading activity. For the last 100 image loads, this returns:

renpy.get_line_log.desc: Returns the list of lines that have been shown since the last time

renpy.get_menu_args.desc: Returns a tuple giving the arguments (as a tuple) and the keyword arguments (as a dict) passed to the current menu statement.

renpy.get_mode.desc: Returns the current mode, or None if it is not defined.

renpy.get_mouse_name.desc: Returns the name of the mouse that should be shown.

renpy.get_mouse_names.desc: Return a list of mouse names that may be displayed, in priority order.

renpy.get_mouse_pos.desc: Returns an (x, y) tuple giving the location of the mouse pointer or the current touch location. If the device does not support a mouse and is not currently being touched, x and y are numbers, but not meaningful.

renpy.get_on_battery.desc: Returns True if Ren'Py is running on a device that is powered by an internal battery, or False if the device is being charged by some external source.

renpy.get_ongoing_transition.desc: Returns the transition that is currently ongoing.

renpy.get_physical_size.desc: Returns the size of the physical window.

renpy.get_placement.desc: This gets the placement of displayable d. There's very little warranty on this information, as it might change when the displayable is rendered, and might not exist until the displayable is first rendered.

renpy.get_refresh_rate.desc: Returns the refresh rate of the current screen, as a floating-point number of frames per second.

renpy.get_renderer_info.desc: Returns a dictionary, giving information about the renderer Ren'Py is currently using. Defined keys are:

renpy.get_return_stack.desc: Returns a list giving the current return stack. The return stack is a list of statement names.

renpy.get_say_attributes.desc: Gets the attributes associated with the current say statement, or None if no attributes are associated with this statement.

renpy.get_say_image_tag.desc: Returns the tag corresponding to the currently speaking character (the `image` argument given to that character). Returns None if no character is speaking or the current speaking character does not have a corresponding image tag.

renpy.get_sdl_dll.desc: Returns a ctypes.cdll object that refers to the library that contains the instance of SDL3 that Ren'Py is using. If this fails, None is returned.

renpy.get_sdl_window_pointer.desc: Returns a pointer to the main window, or None if the main window is not displayed (or some other problem occurs).

renpy.get_showing_tags.desc: Returns the set of image tags that are currently being shown on `layer`. If sort is true, returns a list of the tags from back to front.

renpy.get_side_image.desc: This attempts to find an image to show as the side image.

renpy.get_skipping.desc: Returns "slow" if the Ren'Py is skipping, "fast" if Ren'Py is fast skipping, and None if it is not skipping.

renpy.get_statement_info.desc: Returns a `StatementInfo` object describing the statement that is currently executing or being predicted. This can be called from the predict function of a creator-defined statement.

renpy.get_statement_name.desc: Get the name of the current statement, a string like "say", "say-nvl", or "window hide". This is the same statement name used with `config.statement_callbacks`.

renpy.get_texture_size.desc: Returns the number of bytes of memory locked up in OpenGL textures and the number of textures that are defined.

renpy.get_transition.desc: Gets the transition for `layer`, or the entire scene if `layer` is None. This returns the transition that is queued up to run during the next interaction, or None if no such transition exists.

renpy.get_user_age.desc: Returns a range of ages for the user, if such can be determined. It returns a tuple of two integers, giving the minimum and maximum age of the user. If the age cannot be determined, it returns (-1, 150).

renpy.get_zorder_list.desc: Returns a list of (tag, zorder) pairs for `layer`.

renpy.has_label.desc: Returns true if `name` is a valid label in the program, or false otherwise.

renpy.hide.desc: Hides an image from a layer. The Python equivalent of the hide statement.

renpy.image.desc: Defines an image. This function is the Python equivalent of the image statement.

renpy.image_size.desc: Given an image manipulator, loads it and returns a (`width`, `height`) tuple giving its size.

renpy.imagemap.desc: Displays an imagemap. An image map consists of two images and a list of hotspots that are defined on that image. When the user clicks on a hotspot, the value associated with that hotspot is returned.
renpy.imagemap.signature: (ground, selected, hotspots, unselected=None, overlays=False, style='imagemap', mouse='imagemap', with_none=None, **properties)

renpy.in_fixed_rollback.desc: Returns true if rollback is currently occurring and the current context is before an executed renpy.fix_rollback() statement.

renpy.in_rollback.desc: Returns true if the game has been rolled back.

renpy.include_module.desc: Similar to `renpy.load_module`, but instead of loading the module right away, inserts it into the init queue somewhere after the current AST node.

renpy.input.desc: Calling this function pops up a window asking the player to enter some text. It returns the entered text.
renpy.input.signature: (default='', allow=None, exclude='{}', length=None, pixel_width=None, screen="input", mask=None, copypaste=True, multiline=False, **kwargs)

renpy.invoke_in_main_thread.desc: This runs the given function with the given arguments in the main thread. The function runs in an interaction context similar to an event handler. This is meant to be called from a separate thread, whose creation is handled by `renpy.invoke_in_thread`.

renpy.invoke_in_thread.desc: Invokes the function `fn` in a background thread, passing it the provided arguments and keyword arguments. Restarts the interaction once the thread returns.

renpy.ios.desc: Has a true value when running on iOS.

renpy.is_in_test.desc: Returns True if Ren'py is currently executing a test. This always returns False at init time.

renpy.is_init_phase.desc: Returns True if Ren'Py is currently executing init code, or False otherwise.

renpy.is_mouse_visible.desc: Returns True if the mouse cursor is visible, False otherwise.

renpy.is_pixel_opaque.desc: Returns whether the pixel at (x, y) is opaque when this displayable is rendered by `renpy.render(d, width, height, st, at)`.
renpy.is_pixel_opaque.signature: (d, width, height, st, at, x, y)

renpy.is_seen.desc: Returns true if the current line has been seen by the player.

renpy.is_seen_allowed.desc: Returns False only if in a replay and no seen events allowed by setting `config.no_replay_seen` to True.

renpy.is_skipping.desc: Returns True if Ren'Py is currently skipping (in fast or slow skip mode), or False otherwise.

renpy.is_start_interact.desc: Returns True if restart_interaction has not been called during the current interaction. This can be used to determine if the interaction is just being started, or has been restarted.

renpy.is_warping.desc: Returns True while Ren'Py is reconstructing the state preceding a warp target. A custom say callable with a `warp` attribute set to True can use this to update dialogue state without interacting with the player.

renpy.jump.desc: Causes the current statement to end, and control to jump to the given label.

renpy.jump_out_of_context.desc: Causes control to leave the current context, and then to be transferred in the parent context to the given label.

renpy.last_say.desc: Returns an object containing information about the last say statement.

renpy.license.desc: A string giving license text that should be included in a game's about screen.

renpy.linux.desc: Has a true value when running on Linux or other POSIX-like operating systems.

renpy.list_files.desc: Lists the files in the game directory and archive files. Returns a list of files, with / as the directory separator.

renpy.load_language.desc: (Here because of commonality with load_string and load_module.)

renpy.load_module.desc: This loads the Ren'Py module named name. A Ren'Py module consists of Ren'Py script that is loaded into the usual (store) namespace, contained in a file named name.rpym or name.rpymc. If a .rpym file exists, and is newer than the corresponding .rpymc file, it is loaded and a new .rpymc file is created.

renpy.load_string.desc: Loads `s` as Ren'Py script that can be called.

renpy.loadable.desc: Returns True if the given filename is loadable, meaning that it can be loaded from the disk or from inside an archive. Returns False if this is not the case.

renpy.log.desc: If `config.log` is not set, this does nothing. Otherwise, it opens the logfile (if not already open), formats the message to `config.log_width` columns, and prints it to the logfile.

renpy.macintosh.desc: Has a true value when running on macOS.

renpy.mark_audio_seen.desc: Marks the given filename as if it has been already played on the current user's system.

renpy.mark_audio_unseen.desc: Marks the given filename as if it has not been played on the current user's system yet.

renpy.mark_image_seen.desc: Marks the named image as if it has been already displayed on the current user's system.

renpy.mark_image_unseen.desc: Marks the named image as if it has not been displayed on the current user's system yet.

renpy.mark_label_seen.desc: Marks the named label as if it has been already executed on the current user's system.

renpy.mark_label_unseen.desc: Marks the named label as if it has not been executed on the current user's system yet.

renpy.mark_translation_seen.desc: Marks the translation with the given tlid as seen. `tlid` A string giving the translation id.

renpy.mark_translation_unseen.desc: Marks the translation with the given tlid as not seen.

renpy.maximum_framerate.desc: Forces Ren'Py to draw the screen at the maximum framerate for `t` seconds. If `t` is None, cancels the maximum framerate request.

renpy.menu.desc: Displays a menu, and returns to the user the value of the selected choice. Also handles conditions and the menuset.

renpy.mobile.desc: Has a true value when running on Android or iOS or in the browser.

renpy.mode.desc: Causes Ren'Py to enter the named mode, or stay in that mode if it's already in it.

renpy.movie_cutscene.desc: This displays a movie cutscene for the specified number of seconds. The user can click to interrupt the cutscene. Overlays and Underlays are disabled for the duration of the cutscene.

renpy.music.desc: The renpy.audio.music namespace contains functions that control the `audio system <audio>`. These functions work with the music channel by default.

renpy.music.channel_defined.desc: Returns True if the channel exists, or False otherwise.

renpy.music.get_all_mixers.desc: This gets all mixers in use.

renpy.music.get_delay.desc: Returns the number of seconds left until the given time in the

renpy.music.get_duration.desc: Returns the duration of the audio or video file on `channel`. Returns 0.0 if no file is playing on `channel`, or the duration is unknown. Some formats - notably MP3 - do not include duration information in a format Ren'Py can access.

renpy.music.get_loop.desc: Return a list of filenames that are being looped on `channel`, or None if no files are being looped. In the case where a loop is queued, but is not yet playing, the loop is returned, not the currently playing music.

renpy.music.get_playing.desc: If the given channel is playing, returns the playing file name. Otherwise, returns None.

renpy.music.get_pos.desc: Returns the current position of the audio or video file on `channel`, in seconds. Returns None if no audio is playing on `channel`.

renpy.music.get_state.desc: Returns the lifecycle state of the channel as one of `idle`, `playing`, `paused`, or `ended`. `ended` means natural EOF was reached while the backend may retain the decoder for an explicit seek.

renpy.music.is_music.desc: Returns true if "channel" will loop by default.

renpy.music.is_playing.desc: Returns True if the channel is currently playing a sound, False if it is not, or if the sound system isn't working.

renpy.music.play.desc: This stops the music currently playing on the numbered channel, dequeues any queued music, and begins playing the specified file or files.
renpy.music.play.signature: (filenames, channel='music', loop=None, fadeout=None, synchro_start=None, fadein=0, tight=None, if_changed=False, relative_volume=1.0)

renpy.music.playable.desc: Return true if the given filename is playable on the channel. This

renpy.music.pump.desc: This 'pumps' the audio system. Normally, the effects of the `play`, `queue`, and `stop` statements and the function equivalents take place at the start of the next interaction. In some cases, the effects of multiple statements can cancel each other out - for example, a play followed by a stop causes the track to never be played.

renpy.music.queue.desc: This queues the given filenames on the specified channel.
renpy.music.queue.signature: (filenames, channel='music', loop=None, clear_queue=True, fadein=0, tight=None, relative_volume=1.0)

renpy.music.seek.desc: Seeks the media currently playing on `channel` to `position` seconds. This preserves the active decoder and queued tracks, unlike restarting playback with an audio `<from ...>` specifier. If no media is playing, this function has no effect. Negative positions are treated as zero.

renpy.music.set_audio_filter.desc: Sets the audio filter for sounds about to be queued to `audio_filter`.

renpy.music.set_mixer.desc: This sets the name of the mixer associated with a given channel. By default, there are two mixers, 'sfx' and 'music'. 'sfx' is on channels 0 to 3, and 'music' on 3 to 7. The voice module calls this function to set channel 2 to voice. You can create your own mixer, but will need to add a preference if you wish to allow the user to set it.

renpy.music.set_music.desc: Determines if channel will loop by default.

renpy.music.set_pan.desc: Sets the pan of this channel.

renpy.music.set_pause.desc: Sets the pause flag for `channel` to `value`. If True, the channel will pause, otherwise it will play normally.

renpy.music.set_queue_empty_callback.desc: This sets a callback that is called when the queue is empty. This callback is called when the queue first becomes empty, and at least once per interaction while the queue is empty.

renpy.music.set_volume.desc: Sets the volume of this channel, as a fraction of the volume of the mixer controlling the channel.

renpy.music.stop.desc: This stops the music that is currently playing, and dequeues all queued music. If fadeout is None, the music is faded out for the time given in config.fadeout_audio, otherwise it is faded for fadeout seconds.

renpy.music_start.desc: Deprecated music start function, retained for compatibility. Use

renpy.music_stop.desc: Deprecated music stop function, retained for compatibility. Use

renpy.notify.desc: Causes Ren'Py to display the `message` using the notify screen. By default, this will cause the message to be dissolved in, displayed for two seconds, and dissolved out again.

renpy.notl_file.desc: Like file, but doesn't search the translation prefix.

renpy.open_file.desc: Returns a read-only file-like object that accesses the file named `fn`. The file is accessed using Ren'Py's standard search method, and may reside in the game directory, in an RPA archive, or as an Android asset.

renpy.open_url.desc: Opens a URL in the system's web browser, if possible.

renpy.pause.desc: Causes Ren'Py to pause. Returns true if the user clicked to end the pause, or false if the pause timed out or was skipped.

renpy.play.desc: Plays a sound effect. If `channel` is None, it defaults to styles, `hover_sound` and `activate_sound`.

renpy.pop_call.desc: Pops the current call from the call stack, without returning to the location. Also reverts the values of `dynamic <renpy.dynamic>` variables, the same way the Ren'Py return statement would.

renpy.predict_menu.desc: Predicts widgets that are used by the menu.

renpy.predict_say.desc: This is called to predict the results of a say command.

renpy.predict_show.desc: Predicts a scene or show statement.

renpy.predicting.desc: Returns True if Ren'Py is currently in a predicting phase.

renpy.put_clipboard_data.desc: Sets up clipboard data for multiple MIME types.

renpy.put_clipboard_image_file.desc: Copies an image file to the system clipboard. The image is placed on the clipboard in its original format, and also as a PNG if the original is not already a PNG.

renpy.put_clipboard_text_file.desc: Copies a text file to the system clipboard as a text/plain attachment.

renpy.quit.desc: This causes Ren'Py to exit entirely.

renpy.quit_event.desc: Triggers a quit event, as if the player clicked the quit button in the window chrome.

renpy.redraw.desc: Causes the displayable `d` to be redrawn (the render method called) when `when` seconds have elapsed. The displayable may be redrawn before that time (for example, when a child is redrawn), in which case a pending redraw is forgotten.

renpy.reload_script.desc: Causes Ren'Py to save the game, reload the script, and then load the save.

renpy.render_to_file.desc: Renders a displayable or Render, and saves the result of that render to a file. The render is performed by Ren'Py's display system, such that if the window is upscaled the render will be upscaled as well.
renpy.render_to_file.signature: (d, filename, width=None, height=None, st=0.0, at=None, resize=False)

renpy.render_to_surface.desc: This takes a displayable or Render, and returns a pygame Surface. The render is performed by Ren'Py's display system, such that if the window is upscaled the render will be upscaled as well.

renpy.renpy_pure.desc: Marks renpy.`fn` as a pure function.

renpy.request_permission.desc: Asks Android to grant a permission to this application. The user may be prompted to grant the permission.

renpy.reset_physical_size.desc: Attempts to set the size of the physical window to the size specified using `renpy.config.physical_height` and `renpy.config.physical_width`, or, if those are not set, the size set using `renpy.config.screen_width` and `renpy.config.screen_height`.

renpy.restart_interaction.desc: Restarts the current interaction. Among other things, this displays images added to the scene, re-evaluates screens, and starts any queued transitions.

renpy.retain_after_load.desc: Causes data modified between the current statement and the statement containing the next checkpoint to be retained when a load occurs.

renpy.return_statement.desc: Causes Ren'Py to return from the current Ren'Py-level call.

renpy.roll_forward_core.desc: To cause a roll_forward to occur, return the value of this function from an event handler.

renpy.roll_forward_info.desc: When in rollback, returns the data that was supplied to `renpy.checkpoint` the last time this statement executed. Outside of rollback, returns None.

renpy.rollback.desc: Rolls the state of the game back to the last checkpoint.

renpy.save_persistent.desc: Saves the persistent data to disk.

renpy.say.desc: The equivalent of the say statement.

renpy.scene.desc: Removes all displayables from `layer`. This is equivalent to the scene statement, when the scene statement is not given an image to show.

renpy.screenshot_to_bytes.desc: Returns a screenshot as a bytes object, that can be passed to im.Data(). The bytes will be a png-format image, such that::

renpy.scry.desc: Returns the scry object for the current statement. Returns None if there are no statements executing.

renpy.scry_say.desc: Called when scry is called on a say statement. Needs to set the interacts field.

renpy.seen_audio.desc: Returns True if the given filename has been played at least once on the current user's system.

renpy.seen_image.desc: Returns True if the named image has been seen at least once on the user's system. An image has been seen if it's been displayed using the show statement, scene statement, or `renpy.show` function. (Note that there are cases where the user won't actually see the image, like a show immediately followed by a hide.)

renpy.seen_label.desc: Returns true if the named label has executed at least once on the current user's system, and false otherwise. This can be used to unlock scene galleries, for example.

renpy.seen_translation.desc: Returns True if the translation with the given tlid has been seen at least once.

renpy.set_autoreload.desc: Sets the autoreload flag, which determines if the game will be automatically reloaded after file changes. Autoreload will not be fully enabled until the game is reloaded with `renpy.reload_script`.

renpy.set_editable_input_value.desc: Sets the currently active input value, and if it should be marked as editable.

renpy.set_focus.desc: This attempts to focus the displayable with `id` in the screen `screen`. Focusing will fail if the displayable isn't found, the window isn't focused, or something else is grabbing focus.

renpy.set_mouse_pos.desc: Jump the mouse pointer to the location given by arguments x and y. If the device does not have a mouse pointer, or if it is not possible for Ren'Py to move that pointer, this does nothing.

renpy.set_physical_size.desc: Attempts to set the size of the physical window to `size`. This has the side effect of taking the screen out of fullscreen mode.

renpy.set_return_stack.desc: Sets the current return stack. The return stack is a list of statement names.

renpy.set_tag_attributes.desc: This sets the attributes associated with an image tag when that image tag is not showing. The main use of this would be to directly set the attributes used by a side image.

renpy.show.desc: Shows an image on a layer. This is the programmatic equivalent of the show statement.
renpy.show.signature: (name, at_list=[], layer=None, what=None, zorder=0, tag=None, behind=[], atl=None, **kwargs)

renpy.show_layer_at.desc: The Python equivalent of the `show layer` `layer` `at` `at_list` statement. If `camera` is True, the equivalent of the `camera` statement.

renpy.showing.desc: Returns true if an image with the same tag as `name` is showing on `layer`.

renpy.shown_window.desc: Call this to indicate that the window has been shown. This interacts with the "window show" statement, which shows an empty window whenever this functions has not been called during an interaction.

renpy.sound.desc: The renpy.audio.sound namespace contains functions that control the `audio system <audio>`. These functions work with the sound channel by default. Most functions are documented under their renpy.music equivalents.

renpy.start_predict.desc: This function takes one or more displayables as arguments. It causes Ren'Py to predict those displayables during every interaction until the displayables are removed by `renpy.stop_predict`.

renpy.start_predict_screen.desc: Causes Ren'Py to start predicting the screen named `_screen_name` with the given arguments. This replaces any previous prediction of `_screen_name`. To stop predicting a screen, call `renpy.stop_predict_screen`.

renpy.start_predict_shader.desc: Causes Ren'Py to predict the specified combination of shaders during every interaction until it is removed by `renpy.stop_predict_shader`.

renpy.stop_predict.desc: This function takes one or more displayables as arguments. It causes Ren'Py to stop predicting those displayables during every interaction.

renpy.stop_predict_screen.desc: Causes Ren'Py to stop predicting the screen named `name`.

renpy.stop_predict_shader.desc: Causes Ren'Py to stop predicting the specified combination of shaders during every interaction.

renpy.stop_skipping.desc: Stops skipping, if Ren'Py is currently skipping.

renpy.substitute.desc: Applies translation and new-style formatting to the string `s`.

renpy.suspend_rollback.desc: Rollback will skip sections of the game where rollback has been suspended.

renpy.take_screenshot.desc: Causes a screenshot to be taken. This screenshot will be saved as part of a saved game.

renpy.timeout.desc: Causes an event to be generated before `seconds` seconds have elapsed. This ensures that the event method of a user-defined displayable will be called.

renpy.transition.desc: Sets the transition that will be used during the next interaction.

renpy.utter_restart.desc: Causes an utter restart of Ren'Py. This reloads the script and re-runs initialization.

renpy.variant.desc: Returns true if `name` is a screen variant that corresponds to the context in which Ren'Py is currently executing. See `screen-variants` for more details. This function can be used as the condition in an if statement to switch behavior based on the selected screen variant.

renpy.version_name.desc: A human-readable version name, of the form "Example Version."

renpy.version_only.desc: The version number of Ren'Py, without the Ren'Py prefix. A string of the form "1.2.3.456".

renpy.version_string.desc: The version number of Ren'Py, as a string of the form "Ren'Py 1.2.3.456".

renpy.version_tuple.desc: The version number of Ren'Py, as a tuple of the form (1, 2, 3, 456).

renpy.vibrate.desc: Causes the device to vibrate for `duration` seconds. Currently, this is only supported on Android.

renpy.warp_to_line.desc: This takes as an argument a filename:linenumber pair, and tries to warp to the statement before that line number.

renpy.web_input.desc: This provides input in the web environment, when config.web_input is True.

renpy.windows.desc: Has a true value when running on Windows.

renpy.with_statement.desc: Causes a transition to occur. This is the Python equivalent of the with statement.

reset.desc: Resets the transform to the default values of each property, removing any properites set before it.

rest_indent.desc: Specifies the number of pixels the second and later lines in a paragraph are indented by.

right.desc: Aligns to the bottom-right corner of the screen.

right_bar.desc: The displayable used for the right side of the bar.

right_gutter.desc: The size of the gutter on the right side of the bar, in pixels.

right_margin.desc: The amount of transparent space to the right of the displayable, in pixels.

right_padding.desc: The amount of space between the background and the right side of the window content, in pixels.

ruby_line_leading.desc: The number of pixels of spacing to include above each line that contains `ruby text <ruby-text>`. This is in addition to `line_leading`.

ruby_style.desc: If not None, this should be a style object. The style that's used for ruby text.

save_name.desc: A save name that is included with saves. This is also used by the steam timeline if `config.automatic_steam_timeline` is true, and is best considered to be a chapter name.

say : Callable.desc: A function that is called by Ren'Py to display dialogue, when a string is used in place of the speaking character::

shader.desc: :type: None or str or list of str :default: None

shaper.desc: The shaper used on text. This should be one of "harfbuzz" or "freetype". The harfbuzz shaper is more capable but only works on Ren'Py 8, while "freetype" works in Ren'Py 7 as well.

size.desc: The size of the font on the screen. While this is nominally in pixels, font files may have creative interpretations of this value.

size_group.desc: If not None, this should be a string. Ren'Py will render all windows with the same size_group value at the same size.

slow_abortable.desc: If True, a click that reaches the Text object will cause the slow text to abort, which means that the rest of the slow text will be displayed instantly.

slow_cps.desc: If a number, shows text at the rate of that many characters per second. If True, shows text at the speed taken from the "Text Speed" preference.

slow_cps_multiplier.desc: The speed of the text is multiplied by this number. This can be used to have a character that speaks at a faster-than-normal rate of speed.

spacing.desc: The spacing between members of this box, in pixels.

squares.desc: Transitions the screen in a squares effect lasting 1 second.

strikethrough.desc: If True, a line is drawn through the text.

style.desc: The style namespace contains styles and functions that manipulate styles. Styles are used to control the appearance of text, images, and other elements in Ren'Py. Using the `style` statement is preferred to using the style namespace directly.

style.rebuild.desc: This causes named styles to be rebuilt, allowing styles to be changed after the init phase has finished.

textalign.desc: This is used when a line is shorter than the width of the text displayable. It determines how much of the extra space is placed on the left side of the text. (And hence, the text alignment.)

thumb.desc: If not None, this is a displayable that is drawn over the break between the sides of the bar.

thumb_align.desc: The alignment of the bar thumb, relative to the bar. If the bar and thumb are different sizes - for example, the thumb is taller than the height of a horizontal bar - thumb_align can be set to 0.5 so the centers of the bar and thumb are aligned.

thumb_offset.desc: The amount that by which the thumb overlaps the bars, in pixels. To have the left and right bars continue unbroken, set this to half the width of the thumb in pixels. This may also be a tuple, in which case the first number is used for the left/top thumb offset, and the second number is used for the right/bottom thumb offset.

thumb_shadow.desc: If not None, this is a displayable that is drawn over the break between the sides of the bar.

top.desc: Centers horizontally, and aligns to the top of the screen.

top_bar.desc: The displayable used for the top side of the bar.

top_gutter.desc: The size of the gutter on the top side of the bar, in pixels.

top_margin.desc: The amount of transparent space above the displayable, in pixels.

top_padding.desc: The amount of space between the background and the top side of the window content, in pixels.

topleft.desc: Aligns to the top-left corner of the screen.

topright.desc: Aligns to the top-right corner of the screen.

translate_define.desc: This is used to set a define when generating a game. For example, it can be used to change the size of a font.

translate_font.desc: This is used to set a font for `language`. The font is used in the launcher, and also used to in games generated in that language. The font file should be placed in game/fonts.

ui.desc: *Note: Most functions in the ui namespace are deprecated.*

underline.desc: If True, an underline will be added to the text.

unscrollable.desc: Controls what happens if the bar is unscrollable (if the range is set to 0, as is the case with a viewport containing a displayable smaller than itself). There are three possible values:

updater.desc: The updater namespace contains functions, classes, and variables that control the `HTTP/HTTPS <updater>`.

vertical.desc: If True, the text will be rendered vertically.

vpunch.desc: When invoked, this transition shakes the screen vertically for a quarter second. Imitating and customizing this transition and `hpunch` is best done using `atl-transitions`.

xalign.desc: Equivalent to setting xpos and xanchor to the same value. This has the effect of placing the displayable at a relative location on the screen, with 0.0 being the left side, 0.5 the center, and 1.0 being the right side.

xanchor.desc: The position of the anchor relative to the left side of the displayable.

xcenter.desc: Equivalent to setting xpos to the value of this property, and xanchor to 0.5.

xfail.desc: If this expression evaluates to `True`, the test is expected to fail. If the test does fail, it will be marked as xfailed instead of failed. Defaults to `False`.

xfill.desc: If true, the displayable will expand to fill all available horizontal space. If not true, it will only be large enough to contain its children.

xfit.desc: If True, the size of the fixed layout is shrunk horizontally to match the right side of the rightmost child of the fixed.

xmargin.desc: Equivalent to setting left_margin and right_margin to the same value.

xmaximum.desc: Specifies the maximum horizontal size of the displayable, in pixels.

xminimum.desc: Sets the minimum width of the displayable, in pixels. Only works with displayables that can vary their size.

xoffset.desc: Gives a number of pixels that are added to the horizontal position computed using xpos and xalign.

xpadding.desc: Equivalent to setting left_padding and right_padding to the same value.

xpos.desc: The position of the displayable relative to the left side of the containing area.

xsize.desc: Equivalent to setting xminimum and xmaximum to the same value. This has the effect of setting the width of the displayable. f the size is a float, it's relative to the width of the containing area.

xspacing.desc: The spacing between cells of the grid in the horizontal direction, in pixels. This takes precedence over the spacing property when it is not None.

xycenter.desc: Equivalent to setting xcenter to the first component of the tuple, and ycenter to the second.

xysize.desc: Equivalent to setting xsize to the first component of the tuple, and ysize to the second component.
xysize.signature: tuple of (int or float, int or float)

yalign.desc: Equivalent to setting ypos and yanchor to the same value. This has the effect of placing the displayable at a relative location on the screen, with 0.0 being the top, 0.5 the center, and 1.0 the bottom.

yanchor.desc: The position of the anchor relative to the top side of the displayable.

ycenter.desc: Equivalent to setting ypos to the value of this property, and yanchor to 0.5.

yfill.desc: If true, the displayable will expand to fill all available vertical space. If not true, it will only be large enough to contain its children.

yfit.desc: If True, the size of the fixed layout is shrunk vertically to match the bottom side of the bottommost child of the fixed.

ymargin.desc: Equivalent to setting top_margin and bottom_margin to the same value.

ymaximum.desc: Specifies the maximum vertical size of the displayable in pixels.

yminimum.desc: Sets the minimum height of the displayables, in pixels. Only works with displayables that can vary their size.

yoffset.desc: Gives a number of pixels that are added to the vertical position computed using ypos and yalign.

ypadding.desc: Equivalent to setting top_padding and bottom_padding to the same value.

ypos.desc: The position of the displayable relative to the top side of the containing area.

ysize.desc: Equivalent to setting yminimum and ymaximum to the same value. This has the effect of setting the height of the displayable. If the size is a float, it's relative to the height of the containing area.

yspacing.desc: The spacing between cells of the grid in the vertical direction, in pixels. This takes precedence over the spacing property when it is not None.

zoomin.desc: This zooms in entering images, taking 0.5 seconds to do so.

zoominout.desc: This zooms in entering images and zooms out leaving images, taking 0.5 seconds to do so.

zoomout.desc: This zooms out leaving images, taking 0.5 seconds to do so.
